<h2 id="introduction">Introduction</h2>
<p>The 4D Labs family of embedded graphics processors are powered by a highly optimised soft-core virtual engine, E.V.E. (Extensible Virtual Engine). EVE was designed and created by 4D Labs in the early 2000’s and should not be confused by FTDI’s solution of EVE, which was developed a decent decade or so later.</p>
<p>EVE is a proprietary, high performance virtual processor with an extensive byte-code instruction set optimised to execute compiled 4DGL programs. 4DGL (4D Graphics Language) was specifically developed from ground up for the EVE engine core. It is a high-level language which is easy to learn and simple to understand yet powerful enough to tackle many embedded graphics applications.</p>
<p>4DGL is a graphics-oriented language allowing rapid application development. An extensive library of graphics, text and file system functions and the ease of use of a language that combines the best elements and syntax structure of languages such as C, Basic, Pascal, etc. Programmers familiar with these languages will feel right at home with 4DGL. It includes many familiar instructions such as <code>IF..ELSE..ENDIF, WHILE..WEND, REPEAT..UNTIL, GOSUB..ENDSUB, GOTO</code> as well as a wealth of (chip-resident) internal functions that include <code>SERIN, SEROUT, GFX_LINE, GFX_CIRCLE</code> and many more.</p>
<p>This document covers the internal (chip-resident) functions available for the DIABLO-16 Processor. This document should be used in conjunction with the <a href="../">4DGL Programmers Reference Manual</a>.</p>

<h3 id="isdigit">isdigit</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII digit else returns a 0. Valid range: "0123456789".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>isdigit(char);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:   0 if character is not as ASCII digit, 1 if character is an ASCII digit.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="isxdigit">isxdigit</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII hexadecimal digit else returns a 0.
Valid range: "0123456789ABCDEF".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>isxdigit(char);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if character is not as ASCII hexadecimal digit, 1 if characted is an ASCII hexadecimal digit. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:  Refer to <a href="#isdigit">isdigit Example</a></p>
<h3 id="isupper">isupper</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and returns a 1 if the character is an ASCII upper case letter else returns a 0.
Valid range: "ABCDEF....WXYZ".</p>

<h3 id="toupper">toupper</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and if the character is a lower cases letter, it returns the upper case equivalent else returns the passed char. Valid range: "abcd ... wxyz".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>toupper(char);</code></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="tolower">tolower</h3>
<p>Tests the character parameter and if the character is a lower case letter it returns the upper case equivalent else returns the passed char.
Valid range: "ABCD ... WXYZ".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>toupper(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the ASCII character for the test.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:   The lower case equivalent if characters are upper case else returns the passed char.</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="crc-functions">CRC Functions</h2>
<p>The CRC functions are mainly designed for serial communications, but are implemented in such a way that they can be used to other things as well.
The <a href="#com_txblock">com_TXblock</a> and <a href="#com_rxblock">com_RXblock</a> commands can be used to assist with reading and writing comm ports,
generating and checking CRCs with the minimum of user data manipulation.</p>
<h3 id="crc_16">crc_16</h3>
<p>Calculates the Checksum CRC using the ‘standard’ 16-bit CRC algorithm.
For the standard test string "123456789", crc_16 will return 0xBB3D.
Note if you calculate all of the incoming data INCLUDING the CRC, the result should be 0x00</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>crc_16(buf, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source memory buffer. This is a string pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be used to generate the CRC.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The generated 16-bit CRC.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-6-1" name="__codelineno-6-1" href="#__codelineno-6-1"></a><span class="nl">Crc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">crc_16</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="crc_ccitt">crc_CCITT</h3>
<p>Calculates the Checksum CRC as a ‘standard’ CRCITT checksum.
For the standard test string "123456789", crc_CCITT with seed = 0 (XMODEM protocol) will return = 0x31C3,
for seed = 0xFFFF, the result will be 0x29B1 and for seed = 0x1D0F, the result is 0xE5CC.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>crc_CCITT(buf, count, seed);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source memory buffer. This is a string pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be used to generate the CRC.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">seed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The seed for the CRC generation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The generated CCITT CRC.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-7-1" name="__codelineno-7-1" href="#__codelineno-7-1"></a><span class="nl">Crc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">crc_CCITT</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x0000</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="crc_csum_8">crc_CSUM_8</h3>
<p>Calculates the Checksum CRC as an 8-bit number. This is equivalent to simple addition of all bytes and returning the negated sum an 8-bit value.</p>
<p>For the standard test string "123456789", crc_CSUM_8 will return 0x0023.
Note if you calculate all of the incoming data INCLUDING the CRC, the result should be 0x00</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>crc_CSUM_8(buf, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source memory buffer. This is a string pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be used to generate the CRC.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The generated 8-bit checksum CRC.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-8-1" name="__codelineno-8-1" href="#__codelineno-8-1"></a><span class="nl">Crc</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">crc_CSUM_8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">buf</span><span class="p">),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="crc_modbus">crc_MODBUS</h3>
<p>Calculates the Checksum CRC as per the MODBUS standard.</p>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>crc_MODBUS(buf, count);</code></p>

<h3 id="disp_setgram">disp_setGRAM</h3>
<p>Prepares the GRAM area for user access. The lower 16bits of the pixel count in the selected area is returned. This is usually all that is needed unless GRAM area exceeds 256^2. A copy of the 32bit value can be found in GRAM_PIXEL_COUNT_LO and GRAM_PIXEL_COUNT_HI.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>disp_setGRAM(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left of the GRAM window.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom right of the GRAM window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The LO word of the 32-bit pixel count is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-10-1" name="__codelineno-10-1" href="#__codelineno-10-1"></a><span class="n">disp_setGRAM</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">40</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">150</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="disp_init">disp_Init</h3>

<h3 id="file_count">file_Count</h3>
<p>Returns number of files found that match the criteria.
The wild card character '*'matches up with any combination of allowable characters and '?' matches up with any single allowable character.
Filename must be 8.3 format. Long Filenames are not supported. TESTPR~1.4XE for example.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Count(filename);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of files that match the criteria.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-16-1" name="__codelineno-16-1" href="#__codelineno-16-1"></a><span class="nl">count</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Count</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"*.4XE"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Returns number of files with “.4XE”.</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_findfirst">file_FindFirst</h3>
<p>Returns true if at least 1 file exists that satisfies the file argument.
Wildcards are usually used so if file_FindFirst returns true, further tests can be made using file_FindNext(); to find all the files that match the wildcard class. Note that the stream behaviour is the same as file_Dir.
Filename must be 8.3 format. Long Filenames are not supported. TESTPR~1.4XE for example.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_FindFirst(fname);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the file(s) for the search (passed as a string). 8.3 Format</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>:   1 If at least one file exists that satisfies the criteria. 0 If no file satisfies the criteria.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-18-1" name="__codelineno-18-1" href="#__codelineno-18-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">file_FindFirst</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"*.4XE"</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-18-2" name="__codelineno-18-2" href="#__codelineno-18-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"File Found"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-18-3" name="__codelineno-18-3" href="#__codelineno-18-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_findnext">file_FindNext</h3>
<p>Returns true if more file exists that satisfies the file argument that was given for file_FindFirst. Wildcards must be used for file_FindFirst, else this function will always return zero as the only occurrence will have already been found.
Note that the stream behaviour is the same as file_Dir.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_FindNext();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if more files exist that satisfy the criteria set in the file_FindFirst(fname). 0 if no more files satisfy the criteria set in the file_FindFirst(fname)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-19-1" name="__codelineno-19-1" href="#__codelineno-19-1"></a><span class="k">while</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">((</span><span class="n">file_FindNext</span><span class="p">()))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-19-2" name="__codelineno-19-2" href="#__codelineno-19-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">filecount</span><span class="o">++</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-19-3" name="__codelineno-19-3" href="#__codelineno-19-3"></a><span class="n">wend</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="file_close">file_Close</h3>
<p>Returns TRUE if file closed, FALSE if not.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Close();</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">the file handle that was created by <a href="#file_open">file_Open("fname")</a> which is now used as reference (handle) for "fname" for further file functions such as in this function to close the file.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True (1) if file closed, False (0) otherwise.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-21-1" name="__codelineno-21-1" href="#__codelineno-21-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Close</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_open">file_Open</h3>
<p>Returns handle if file exists. The file "<strong>handle</strong>" that is created is now used as reference for "filename" for further file functions such as <a href="#file_close">file_Close(handle)</a>, etc. For <code>FILE_WRITE</code> and <code>FILE_APPEND</code> modes (<code>'w'</code> and <code>'a'</code>) the file is created if it does not exist.</p>
<p>If the file is opened for append and it already exists, the file pointer is set to the end of the file ready for appending, else the file pointer will be set to the start of the newly created file.</p>
<p>If the file was opened successfully, the internal error number is set to 0 (i.e. no errors) and can be read with the <a href="#file_error">file_Error()</a> function.</p>
<p>For <code>FILE_READ</code> mode (<code>'r'</code>) the file must exist else a null handle (0) is returned and the 'file not found' error number is set which can be read with the <a href="#file_error">file_Error()</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Open(fname, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the file(s) for the search (passed as a string). 8.3 Format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><code>FILE_READ</code> (<code>'r'</code>), <code>FILE_WRITE</code> (<code>'w'</code>) or <code>FILE_APPEND</code> (<code>'a'</code>)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Handle if file exists. Sets internal file error number accordingly (0 if no errors).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>If a file is opened for write mode 'w', and the file already exists, the operation will fail. Unlike C and some other languages where the file will be erased ready for re-writing when opened for writing, 4DGL offers a simple level of protection that ensures that a file must be purposely erased before being re-written.</li>
<li>Beginning with the v4.0 PmmC a file opened with FILE_APPEND may be randomly read and or written. Also any altered file will have the Archive bit set in the directory entry.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_read">file_Read</h3>
<p>Reads the number of bytes specified by <strong>size</strong> from the file referenced by <strong>handle</strong> into a destination memory buffer.
Destination is always a word pointer, as you can only read into RAM which is word addressable.
If <strong>destination</strong> is zero, data is read direct to GRAM window.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Read(*destination, size, hanlde);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination memory buffer. Word Pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be read</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file to be read.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of characters read.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-22-1" name="__codelineno-22-1" href="#__codelineno-22-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Read</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">memblock</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl1</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_seek">file_Seek</h3>
<p>Places the file pointer at the required position in a file that has been opened in <code>'r'</code> (read) or <code>'a'</code> (append) mode. In append mode, file_Seek does not expand a filesize, instead, the file pointer (handle) is set to the end position of the file, e.g.:- assuming the file size is 10000 bytes, <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(handle, 0, 0x1234)</a>; will set the file position to 0x00001234 (byte position 4660) for the file handle, so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with <a href="#file_getc">file_GetC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_getw">file_GetW(...)</a>, <a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a>, or an image can be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Conversely, <a href="#file_putc">file_PutC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_putw">file_PutW(...)</a> and <a href="#file_puts">file_PutS(...)</a> can write to the file at the position. A <strong>FE_EOF</strong> (end of file error) will occur if you try to write or read past the end of the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Seek(handle, HiWord, LoWord);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HiWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16bits of the memory pointer into the file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoWord</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16bits of the memory pointer into the file</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if ok, usually ignored.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-23-1" name="__codelineno-23-1" href="#__codelineno-23-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Seek</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x0000</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1234</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_index">file_Index</h3>
<p>Places the file pointer at the position in a file that has been opened in <code>'r'</code> (read) or <code>'a'</code> (append) mode. In append mode, file_Index does not expand a filesize, instead, the file pointer (handle) is set to the end position of the file, e.g.:- assuming the record size is 100 bytes, <a href="#file_index">file_Index(handle, 0, 100, 22)</a>; will set the file position to 2200 for the file handle, so subsequent data may be read from that position onwards with <a href="#file_getc">file_GetC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_getw">file_GetW(...)</a>, <a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a>, or an image can be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Conversely, <a href="#file_putc">file_PutC(...)</a>, <a href="#file_putw">file_PutW(...)</a> and <a href="#file_puts">file_PutS(...)</a> can write to the file at the position. A FE_EOF (end of file error) will occur if you try to write or read past the end of the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Index(handle, Hisize, LoSize, recordnum);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Hisize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the upper 16bits of the size of the file records.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LoSize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Contains the lower 16bits of the size of the file records.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">recordnum</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The index of the required record.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if ok, usually ignored.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:  </p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-24-1" name="__codelineno-24-1" href="#__codelineno-24-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Index</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">22</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_screencapture">file_ScreenCapture</h3>
<p>Save an image of the screen shot to file at the current file position.</p>
<p>The image can later be displayed with <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>; The file may be opened in append mode to accumulate multiple images. Later, the images can be displayed with <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a>.</p>
<p>All image headers must start on a sector boundary.</p>
<p>The image is saved from x, y (with respect to top left corner), and the capture area is determined by "width" and "height".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_ScreenCapture(x, y, width, height, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">X-position of the image to be captured</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Y-position of the image to be captured</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Width of the area to be captured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Height of the area to be captured.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file to store the image(s)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>: Zero (0) if function successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-29-1" name="__codelineno-29-1" href="#__codelineno-29-1"></a><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span>

<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if function succeeded.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-32-1" name="__codelineno-32-1" href="#__codelineno-32-1"></a><span class="n">file_putW</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0x1234</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_getw">file_GetW</h3>
<p>This function reads a word (2 bytes) from the file, at the position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately (incremented by 2). The file must be previously opened with <code>'r'</code> (read) mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_GetW(handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</tr>
</thead>

<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that reference to the file.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The next word in the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_puts">file_PutS</h3>
<p>This function writes an ASCIIZ (null terminated) string from a buffer specified by "<strong>*source</strong>" to the file, at the position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately. The file must be previously opened with <code>'w'</code> (write) or <code>'a'</code> (append) modes.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_PutS(*source, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">source</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A pointer to the string to be written. Word Pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file to be written to.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The number of the characters written (excluding the null terminator).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-34-1" name="__codelineno-34-1" href="#__codelineno-34-1"></a><span class="n">file_PutS</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_gets">file_GetS</h3>
<p>This function reads a line of text to a buffer (specified by "<strong>*string</strong>") from a file at the current file position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately. The file must be previously opened with <code>'r'</code> (read) mode.</p>
<p><strong>file_GetS(...)</strong> will stop reading when any of the following conditions are true:</p>
<p>a. It has read n-1 bytes (one character is reserved for the null-terminator)
b. It encounters a newline character (a line-feed in the compilers tested here)
c. It reaches the end of file
d. A read error occurs.</p>
<p>The file must be previously opened with <code>'r'</code> (read) mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_GetS(*string, size, handle);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination buffer, Word Pointer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The maximum number of bytes to be read from the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The number of characters read from file (excluding the null terminator)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-35-1" name="__codelineno-35-1" href="#__codelineno-35-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_GetS</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Only reads up to "size-1" characters into "string".</p>
</div>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Rewind(handle);</code></p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-37-1" name="__codelineno-37-1" href="#__codelineno-37-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">file_Rewind</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hSource</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_loadfunction">file_LoadFunction</h3>
<p>Load a function or program from disk and return a function pointer to the allocation.</p>
<p>The function can then be invoked just like any other function would be called via a function pointer. Parameters may be passed to it in a conventional way. The function may be discarded at any time when no longer required, thus freeing its memory resources.</p>
<p>The loaded function can be discarded with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(..)</a> Note that any pointer references passed to the child function may not include references to the parents DATA statements or any static string references. Any string or array information must be in the parents global or local memory space. The reason for this is that DATA statements and static strings are contained in the parents CODE segment, and cannot be accessed by the child process.</p>
<p>The callers stack is shared by the loaded function, however any global variables in the loaded function are private to that function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_LoadFunction(fname.4XE);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname.4XE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the 4DGL application program that is about to be loaded into RAM.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the memory allocation where the function has been loaded from file which can be then used as a function call.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--prev" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div><div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--next" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_run">file_Run</h3>
<p>Any memory allocations in the main FLASH program are released, however, the stack and globals are maintained.</p>
<p>If <strong>arglistptr</strong> is 0, no arguments are passed, else <strong>arglistptr</strong> points to an array, the first element being the number of additional elements in the array which contain the arguments.</p>
<p>func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any.</p>
<p>The arguments can only be passed by value, no pointers or references can be used as all memory is cleared before the file is loaded. Refer to file_Exec and file_LoadFunction for functions that can pass by reference.</p>
<p>The disk does not need to be mounted, file_Run automatically mounts the drive.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Run(fname.4XE, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname.4XE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">name of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_exec">file_Exec</h3>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#file_run">file_Run</a>, however, the main program in FLASH retains all memory allocations (e.g. file buffers, memory allocated with mem_Alloc etc).</p>
<p>Returns like a function, current program calling program is kept active and control returns to it.</p>
<p>If <strong>arglistptr</strong> is 0, no arguments are passed, else <strong>arglist</strong> points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array.</p>
<p>func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments.</p>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#file_loadfunction">file_LoadFunction(...)</a>, however, the function argument list is passed by pointer, and the memory consumed by the function is released as soon as the function completes.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_Exec(fname.4XE, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL child program to be loaded into RAM and executed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program or 0 if no arguments.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>

<div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--prev" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div><div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--next" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl</h3>
<p>Reads a control file to create an image list.</p>
<p id="file_loadimagecontrol_modes">The following are the modes of operation</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">It is assumed that there is a graphics file with the file extension "fname2.gci". In this case, the images have been stored in a FAT16 file concurrently, and the offsets that are derived from the "fname1.dat" file are saved in the image control so that the image control can open the file (<em>.gci) and use <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a> to get to the position of the image which can then automatically be displayed using <a href="#file_image">file_Image(...)</a>. Mode 0 builds the image control quickly as it only scans the </em>.dat file for the file offsets and saves them in the relevant entries in the image control. The penalty is that images take longer to find when displayed due to <a href="#file_seek">file_Seek(...)</a> overheads.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">It is assumed that there is a graphics file with the file extension "fname2.gci". In this case, the images have been stored in a FAT16 file concurrently, and the offset of the images are saved in the image control so that image file (*.gci) can be mapped to directly. The absolute cluster/sector is mapped so file seek does not need to be called internally. This means that there is no seek time penalty, however, the image list takes a lot longer to build, as all the seeking is done at control build time.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">In this case, the images have been stored in a in a RAW partition of the uSD card, and the absolute address of the images are saved in the DAT file. This is the fastest operation of the image control as there is no seeking or other disk activity taking place.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">This mode is for Flash based 'file system' GCI (GCIF) with integrated DAT and other file types. "fname1" and "fname2" are then the Flash high and low words of the GCIF start location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>When an image control is loaded, an array is built in RAM. It consists of a 6 word header with the following entries as defined by the constants:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Information</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Index</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_COUNT</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_ENTRYLEN</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_GCI_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_DAT_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_GCIFILE_HANDLE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>No images are stored in FLASH or RAM, the image control holds the index values for the absolute storage positions on the uSD card for RAW mode, or the cluster/sector position for formatted FAT16 mode.</p>
<p>When an image control is no longer required, the memory can be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free()</a>;</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_LoadImageControl(fname1, fname2, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The control list filename "*.dat".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The image filename "*.gci".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Determines the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol_modes">mode of operation</a></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<!-- TODO: Confirm if 'fname1' and 'fname2' accept string (byte-aligned) pointer or array (word-aligned) pointer -->

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: Pointer (handle) to the memory allocation to the image control list that has been created, null (0) if function fails</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_mount">file_Mount</h3>
<p>Starts up the FAT16 disk file services and allocates a small 32 byte control block for subsequent use. When you open a file using <a href="#file_open">file_Open(...)</a>, a further 512 + 44 = 556 bytes are attached to the FAT16 file control block. When you close a file using <a href="#file_close">file_Close(...)</a>, the 556 byte allocation is released leaving the 32 byte file control block. The <a href="#file_mount">file_Mount()</a> function must be called before any other FAT16 file related functions can be used. The control block and all FAT16 file resources are completely released with <a href="#file_unmount">file_Unmount()</a>. </p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_Mount();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: True (1) if successful, False (0) otherwise</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-44-1" name="__codelineno-44-1" href="#__codelineno-44-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">!</span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-2" name="__codelineno-44-2" href="#__codelineno-44-2"></a><span class="w">   </span><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">file_Mount</span><span class="p">()))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-3" name="__codelineno-44-3" href="#__codelineno-44-3"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Disk not mounted"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-4" name="__codelineno-44-4" href="#__codelineno-44-4"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-5" name="__codelineno-44-5" href="#__codelineno-44-5"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-6" name="__codelineno-44-6" href="#__codelineno-44-6"></a><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-7" name="__codelineno-44-7" href="#__codelineno-44-7"></a><span class="w">   </span><span class="n">wend</span>
<a id="__codelineno-44-8" name="__codelineno-44-8" href="#__codelineno-44-8"></a><span class="n">endif</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="file_unmount">file_Unmount</h3>

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-45-1" name="__codelineno-45-1" href="#__codelineno-45-1"></a><span class="n">file_Unmount</span><span class="p">();</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_playwav">file_PlayWAV</h3>
<p>Open the wav file, decode the header to set the appropriate wave player parameters and set off the playing of the file as a background process. See <a href="#sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</a> for additional play control functions.</p>
<p id="file_playwav_err_codes">This function may return the following values if unsuccessful:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Error Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Insufficient memory available for WAV buffer and file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">cant play this rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no data chunk found in first rsector</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no format data</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no wave chunk signature</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">bad wave file format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">file not found</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_setdate">file_SetDate</h3>
<p>This function sets the modified date and time on an open file handle. The file must be closed at some future time for the date and time to be flushed to disk.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>file_SetDate(handle, year, month, day, hour, minute, second) ;</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that reference the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">year</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The year the file was updated 1980-2099.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">month</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The month the file was updated 1 - 12.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">The day the file was updated 1 - 31.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>
</tbody>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="file_checkupdate">file_CheckUpdate</h3>

<p id="file_checkupdate_options">The following options determine the mode of operation:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Option</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_QUERY</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Checks the specified file and compares its DateTime to the program running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATENEWER</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Updates the program in Flash if the program on uSD is newer</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATEALWAYS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Always updates the program in Flash</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p id="file_checkupdate_results">
If update occurs and the program is running from Flash, the display is reset after update.
Otherwise, if a query or an error occurs, the following is returned:
</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: left;">Option</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_NEWFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is newer than the file running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_OLDFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is equal to or older than the file running in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_UPDATEDONE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">An update was performed, and the program is running from RAM</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_NOFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file does not exist</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">CHECKUPDATE_INVALIDFILE</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The specified file is not valid '4xe' or '4fn'</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>file_CheckUpdate(fname, options);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Argument</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">fname</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Filename of the 4DGL program on the uSD card</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><a href="#file_checkupdate_options">options</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Determines whether to update always (3), update if newer (2) or simply query (1)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<p><strong><em>Return</em></strong>: <a href="#file_checkupdate_results">Result of the operation</a></p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="flash-memory-functions">Flash Memory Functions</h2>
<h3 id="flash_bank">flash_Bank</h3>
<p>Identifies which flash bank the code is running from.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_Bank();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The FLASH bank that code is currently running from, 0-5.</p>
<p>0: Flashbank_0 <br>
1: Flashbank_1 <br>
2: Flashbank_2 <br>
3: Flashbank_3 <br>
4: Flashbank_4 <br>
5: Flashbank_5</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-50-1" name="__codelineno-50-1" href="#__codelineno-50-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bank</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-50-2" name="__codelineno-50-2" href="#__codelineno-50-2"></a><span class="nl">bank</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">flash_Bank</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="flash_blit1">flash_Blit1</h3>
<p>Blit an image to a GRAM window from FLASH storage. Image is stored in a linear fashion to suit the GRAM mechanism, palette is 2 x 16bit colours</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_Blit1(bank, offset, count, pallete2colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bank</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Flash bank to load the image from. <br> 0 or FLASHBANK_0 <br> 1 or FLASHBANK_1 <br> 2 or FLASHBANK_2 <br> 3 or FLASHBANK_3 <br> 4 or FLASHBANK_4 <br> 5 or FLASHBANK_5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">offset</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Offset in to the Flash bank where image is stored.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Total number of pixel in the image.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pallete2colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">An array of 2 elements being the colors for the two possible colour values.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Actual count (normally same as count, will be lower if bank bounds exceeded)</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-51-1" name="__codelineno-51-1" href="#__codelineno-51-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">actual_count</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-2" name="__codelineno-51-2" href="#__codelineno-51-2"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">pixels</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2000</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-3" name="__codelineno-51-3" href="#__codelineno-51-3"></a><span class="c1">// pallete should be defined as an array of 2 elements</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-4" name="__codelineno-51-4" href="#__codelineno-51-4"></a><span class="c1">// of 16bit color values</span>
<a id="__codelineno-51-5" name="__codelineno-51-5" href="#__codelineno-51-5"></a><span class="nl">actual_count</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">flash_Blit1</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FLASHBANK_2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">pixels</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">pallete</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="flash_copy">flash_Copy</h3>
<p>Copies bytes from any flash locations to a user buffer. If the bank is read protected, 0 bytes will be read.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_Copy(bank, ptr, dest, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bank</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Flash bank to copy the data from. <br> 0 or FLASHBANK_0 <br> 1 or FLASHBANK_1 <br> 2 or FLASHBANK_2 <br> 3 or FLASHBANK_3 <br> 4 or FLASHBANK_4 <br> 5 or FLASHBANK_5 <br> -1 or ALL to select all the banks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to a location in the selected flash bank.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the destination. The destination pointer is word aligned.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Count of bytes to be transferred.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The count of the bytes transfered.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flash_erasebank">flash_EraseBank</h3>
<p>This function should be used with extreme caution. The selected bank will be completely erased regardless of FLASH_WRITE_PROTECT status if the confirmation value is set to hex 0xDEAD. If confirmation is any other value, a protected bank will not be erased, and function will return with 0 If the destination bank is the same as the execution bank, the processor will reset upon completion of erase. If the "bank" argument is set to ALL (-1) and confirmation is set to 0xDEAD, FLASHBANK_0 through FLASHBANK_5 are cleared.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<ul>
<li>Use with caution, this is a good way to 'clean up' the entire flash when starting new projects.</li>
<li>Reset processor if program is erasing itself, or the ALL bank option is selected.</li>
</ul>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_EraseBank(bank, confirmation);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bank</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Flash bank to be erased. <br> 0 or FLASHBANK_0 <br> 1 or FLASHBANK_1 <br> 2 or FLASHBANK_2 <br> 3 or FLASHBANK_3 <br> 4 or FLASHBANK_4 <br> 5 or FLASHBANK_5 <br> -1 or ALL to select all the banks.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">confirmation</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xDEAD: The command will erase regardless or FLASH_WRITE_PROTECT status. For any other value, a protected bank will not be erased.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if the function succeeded.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-57-1" name="__codelineno-57-1" href="#__codelineno-57-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">flash_EraeBank</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FLASHBANK_2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-57-2" name="__codelineno-57-2" href="#__codelineno-57-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Erased successfully."</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-57-3" name="__codelineno-57-3" href="#__codelineno-57-3"></a><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-57-4" name="__codelineno-57-4" href="#__codelineno-57-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Failed"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-57-5" name="__codelineno-57-5" href="#__codelineno-57-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="flash_exec">flash_Exec</h3>
<p>This function calls the main function in another bank. The main program in FLASH retains all memory allocations (e.g. file buffers, memory allocated with <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc</a> etc.)</p>
<p>The called bank returns like a function, program in current bank is kept active and control returns to it. All memory allocated in the called bank should be freed before returning, or it will be lost.</p>
<p>If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else arglist points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array.</p>
<p>func 'main' in the called bank accepts the arguments.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_Exec(flashbank, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">flashbank</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Name of the bank to be executed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the selected bank or 0 if no arguments.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called bank.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-58-1" name="__codelineno-58-1" href="#__codelineno-58-1"></a><span class="n">flash_Exec</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FLASHBANK_1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flash_functioncall">flash_FunctionCall</h3>
<p>Calls the Flashbank passing index "index" as the first parameter.</p>
<p>Other parameters "State", "&amp;FunctionRam", "&amp;FunctionDef", "&amp;FunctionDef" are passed. The second two parameters are passed "as is", since the third parameter is normally in flash and one banks flash is not accessible from another</p>
<p>"FunctionArgCount" constants are copied into a RAM array and passed to the Function. "FunctionStringMap" is a bit array of the indexes containing single and multiple strings offset by 8. e.g. 0x0100 means parameter 8 is a single string, 0x0002 means paramter 9 is an array of strings with parameter 8 containing the count.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:  <code>flash_FunctionCall(bank, idx, state, FncRam, FncDef, FncArgCnt, FncStrMap);</code> </p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bank</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Flash bank to write the block to. <br> 0 or FLASHBANK_0 <br> 1 or FLASHBANK_1 <br> 2 or FLASHBANK_2 <br> 3 or FLASHBANK_3 <br> 4 or FLASHBANK_4 <br> 5 or FLASHBANK_5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Value passed to update function state</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;FunctionRam</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the function RAM allocation</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;FunctionDef</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the function definitions stored in Flash</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FunctionArgCount</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Function argument count</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FunctionArgStringMap</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String address array</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-65-1" name="__codelineno-65-1" href="#__codelineno-65-1"></a><span class="n">flash_FunctionCall</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bank</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">idx</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">state</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">FncRam</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">FncDef</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">FncArgCnt</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">FncStrMap</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="flash_loadspiflash">flash_LoadSPIflash</h3>
<p>Copies a file from uSD to the required flashbank. The destination bank cannot be the execution bank, or a bank that is write protected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flash_LoadSPIflash (bank, hndl, idx);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bank</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Flash bank to load the file from. <br> 0 or FLASHBANK_0 <br> 1 or FLASHBANK_1 <br> 2 or FLASHBANK_2 <br> 3 or FLASHBANK_3 <br> 4 or FLASHBANK_4 <br> 5 or FLASHBANK_5</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">hndl</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The handle that references the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if the function succeeded</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-66-1" name="__codelineno-66-1" href="#__codelineno-66-1"></a><span class="nl">result</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">flash_LoadSPIflash</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FLASHBANK_2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"TETRIS10.EXE"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// load the file from disk into FLASHBANK_2</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="floating-point-functions">Floating Point Functions</h2>
<h3 id="flt_add">flt_ADD</h3>
<p>Performs floating point addition (A+B) and returns the value in the result register.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_ADD(&amp;result, &amp;floatA, &amp;floatB);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;result</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatA</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatB</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value B.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>Arguments may be a pointer to a float variable or a numeric text string. A string argument is converted at run-time by calling flt_Val for a string argument.</p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the float result register or zero if error occurs. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-67-1" name="__codelineno-67-1" href="#__codelineno-67-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">floatA</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">floatB</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">];</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-2" name="__codelineno-67-2" href="#__codelineno-67-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_ScreenMode</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">LANDSCAPE</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">//landscape orientation</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-3" name="__codelineno-67-3" href="#__codelineno-67-3"></a><span class="n">flt_VAL</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">floatA</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"3.3"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// Convert a string ("3.3") to a floatA</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-4" name="__codelineno-67-4" href="#__codelineno-67-4"></a><span class="n">flt_ITOF</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">floatB</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                </span><span class="c1">//Convert integer "4" to float</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-5" name="__codelineno-67-5" href="#__codelineno-67-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-67-6" name="__codelineno-67-6" href="#__codelineno-67-6"></a><span class="n">flt_ADD</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">floatA</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">floatB</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-7" name="__codelineno-67-7" href="#__codelineno-67-7"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-8" name="__codelineno-67-8" href="#__codelineno-67-8"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"add: "</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-9" name="__codelineno-67-9" href="#__codelineno-67-9"></a><span class="n">flt_PRINT</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"%.6f"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-67-10" name="__codelineno-67-10" href="#__codelineno-67-10"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>A float variable is a 2 word array, e.g. <code>var myfloat[2]</code>.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_sub">flt_SUB</h3>
<p>Performs floating point Subtraction (A-B) and returns the value in the result register.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_SUB(&amp;result, &amp;floatA, &amp;floatB);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;result</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatA</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatB</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value B.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>Arguments may be a pointer to a float variable or a numeric text string. A string argument is converted at run-time by calling flt_Val for a string argument.</p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the float result register or zero if error occurs. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_div">flt_DIV</h3>
<p>Performs floating point Division (A/B) and returns the value in the result register.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_DIV(&amp;result, &amp;floatA, &amp;floatB);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;result</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatA</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value A.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatB</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value B.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the float result register or zero if error occurs. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<p>see the example in <a href="#flt_mul">flt_MUL()</a></p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>A float variable is a 2 word array, e.g. <code>var myfloat[2]</code>.</p>
</div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_cos">flt_COS</h3>
<p>Calculates the COSINE of float value in radians and returns the value in the result register.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_COS(&amp;result, &amp;floatval);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;result</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;floatval</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value angle (in radians) to get the COSINE of.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the float result register or zero if error occurs. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_sgn">flt_SGN</h3>

<td style="text-align: left;">Points to the float value to examine the sign of.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  16bit integer -1 if float sign is negative, or zero if positive.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_ultof">flt_ULTOF</h3>
<p>Converts a 32bit unsigned integer value to a positive floating point number.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_ULTOF(&amp;fresult, uvar32);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result variable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">uvar32</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A 32bit (long) unsigned variable.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The pointer to the float result.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_val">flt_VAL</h3>
<p>Converts the number string to a valid float value. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_VAL(&amp;fresult, numstring);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;fresult</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result variable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">numstring</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant or string variable that holds valid floating point number.The string argument can be a string constant, a pointer to a string variable, or a pointer to a data statement.The string may be a float, or a hex or binary integer value (no decimal point allowed). For hex or binary, the number is preceeded with 0x or 0b.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The pointer to the float result.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<p>See the example in section <a href="#flt_add">flt_ADD</a>.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>A float variable is a 2 word array, e.g. <code>var myfloat[2]</code>.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_print">flt_PRINT</h3>
<p>Prints a floating point value in a set string format.</p>
<p>The string argument can be a string constant, a pointer to a string variable, or a pointer to a data statement. If it is zero or an empty string, the number is automatically formatted for the best presentation. The format string is similar to the C language, but only a single '%' may be used to print a single variable.</p>
<p>To format the output, refer to the following syntax:</p>
<p><img alt="format" src="../img/diablo16/flt_PRINT_format.png"></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">flag</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Left justify.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">+</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Always display Sign.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">space</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Display space if there is no sign.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pad with leading zeros.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong>width</strong> specifies the number of characters used in total to display the value. Notice that the width includes the decimal point, and a - sign if there is one.</p>
<p><strong>precision</strong> indicates the number of characters used after the decimal point.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">specifier</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Meaning</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">f</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Float</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">e or E</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Float exponential Format.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_PRINT(&amp;fvalue, formatstring);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;fresult</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result variable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">formatString</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">zero, null string, of valid format string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  ‘0’ if successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-95-1" name="__codelineno-95-1" href="#__codelineno-95-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">floatA</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">];</span>
<a id="__codelineno-95-2" name="__codelineno-95-2" href="#__codelineno-95-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_ScreenMode</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">LANDSCAPE</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">//landscape orientation </span>
