<h3 class="page-break" id="flt_printxy">flt_PRINTxy</h3>
<p>Prints a floating point value in a set string format at the specified position.</p>
<p>The string argument can be a string constant, a pointer to a string variable, or a pointer to a data statement. If it is zero or an empty string, the number is automatically formatted for the best presentation. The format string is similar to the C language, but only a single '%' may be used to print a single variable.</p>
<p>For more information on the syntax of the format string, refer to section <a href="#flt_print">flt_PRINT (&amp;fvalue, formatstring)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>flt_PRINTxy(x, y, &amp;fvalue, formatstring);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The x position to start printing the number in.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The y position to start printing the number in.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;fresult</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to float result variable.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">formatstring</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">zero, null string, of valid format string</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  ‘0’ if successfull.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-96-1" name="__codelineno-96-1" href="#__codelineno-96-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">floatA</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">];</span>

<p>Stop execution of the user program for a predetermined amount of time.</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">time</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A value specifying the delay time in milliseconds.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-97-1" name="__codelineno-97-1" href="#__codelineno-97-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">status</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// if fire button pressed</span>
<a id="__codelineno-97-2" name="__codelineno-97-2" href="#__codelineno-97-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// slow down the loop</span>
<a id="__codelineno-97-3" name="__codelineno-97-3" href="#__codelineno-97-3"></a><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-97-4" name="__codelineno-97-4" href="#__codelineno-97-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="p">...</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="lookup8">lookup8</h3>
<p>Search a list of 8-bit constant values for a match with a search value <strong>key</strong>. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned in <strong>result</strong>, else <strong>result</strong> is set to zero. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to one. If second in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to two etc. If not found, <strong>result</strong> is returned with zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>lookup8(key, byteConstList);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A byte value to search for in a fixed list of constants. The <strong>key</strong> argument can be a variable, array element, expression or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byteConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants and strings to be matched against <strong>key</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The index of the matching constant, otherwise zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-98-1" name="__codelineno-98-1" href="#__codelineno-98-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>
<a id="__codelineno-98-2" name="__codelineno-98-2" href="#__codelineno-98-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-98-3" name="__codelineno-98-3" href="#__codelineno-98-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-98-4" name="__codelineno-98-4" href="#__codelineno-98-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">key</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'a'</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-98-5" name="__codelineno-98-5" href="#__codelineno-98-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">lookup8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4D</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'Z'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-98-6" name="__codelineno-98-6" href="#__codelineno-98-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">" nSearch value 'a' nfound as index "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-98-7" name="__codelineno-98-7" href="#__codelineno-98-7"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-98-8" name="__codelineno-98-8" href="#__codelineno-98-8"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">key</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-98-9" name="__codelineno-98-9" href="#__codelineno-98-9"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">lookup8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">key</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4D</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"abcd"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="sc">'Z'</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The list of constants cannot be re-directed. The <a href="#lookup8">lookup8(...)</a> functions offer a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This can be very useful for data entry filtering and parameter input checking and where ever you need to check the validity of certain inputs. The entire search list field can be replaced with a single name if you use the $ operator in constant, e.g. :</p>
<p><code>#constant HEXVALUES $"0123456789ABCDEF"</code></p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="lookup16">lookup16</h3>
<p>Search a list of 16-bit constant values for a match with a search value <strong>key</strong>. If found, the index of the matching constant is returned in <strong>result</strong>, else <strong>result</strong> is set to zero. Thus, if the value is found first in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to one. If second in the list, <strong>result</strong> is set to two etc. If not found, <strong>result</strong> is returned with zero.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">key</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A byte value to search for in a fixed list of constants. The <strong>key</strong> argument can be a variable, array element, expression or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">wordConstList</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A comma separated list of constants to be matched against <strong>key</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The index of the matching constant, otherwise zero</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-99-1" name="__codelineno-99-1" href="#__codelineno-99-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">main</span><span class="p">()</span>

<a id="__codelineno-99-6" name="__codelineno-99-6" href="#__codelineno-99-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">//r := lookup16(key,</span>

<a id="__codelineno-99-9" name="__codelineno-99-9" href="#__codelineno-99-9"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Search value 5000 nfound at index "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-99-10" name="__codelineno-99-10" href="#__codelineno-99-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="k">else</span>
<a id="__codelineno-99-11" name="__codelineno-99-11" href="#__codelineno-99-11"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Value not found"</span><span class="p">);</span>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <a href="#lookup16">lookup16(...)</a> functions offer a versatile way for returning an index for a given value. This is very useful for parameter input checking and where ever you need to check the validity of certain values. The entire search list field can be replaced with a single name by using the $ operator in constant, e.g.:</p>
<p><code>#constant LEGALVALS $5,10,20,50,100,200,500,1000,2000,5000,10000</code></p>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If using PIN_AN or PIN_ANAVG via the <a href="#pin-read">pin_Read()</a> function, then if Touch is enabled this function should be called no more than once per millisecond, otherwise touch behaviour could be erratic.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="pin_read">pin_Read</h3>
<p>Read a pin in various ways. If the pin is set to an input, read the state of the input pin. If set to an output, read the state of the output latch. If set to analogue, read the 12 bit analogue value.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="bus_read">bus_Read</h3>
<p>Read the 16-bit port regardless of pin configurations. If a pin is configured as input or analogue, the pin is read directly as if it were a digital input. If a pin is configured as an output, the pin is also read directly, giving the output latch state.</p>

</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PA0</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">61</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">Yes</td>

<td style="text-align: center;">62</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">Yes</td>

<h3 class="page-break" id="bus_read8">bus_Read8</h3>
<p>Returns the state of the bus as an 8bit value in to the lower byte of the assigned variable.</p>
<p>The BUS_RD pin set to LO, then, after a settling delay of approx 50nsec, the BUS is read into the lower 8-bits of the assigned variable (the upper 8-bits being set to 0) the BUS_RD pin is then set back to a HI level.</p>
<p><img alt="bus_Read8" src="../img/diablo16/bus_Read8.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_Read8();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The state of the 8-bit bus as an 8bit value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-106-1" name="__codelineno-106-1" href="#__codelineno-106-1"></a><span class="nl">var1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">bus_Read8</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The lower byte of var1 will get loaded with the state of the bus.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The BUS_RD pin must be preset to the desired output state must the bus pins to ensure BUS write integrity.</p>
<p><code>BUS_RD is PA3</code></p>
<p>The 8-bit BUS pins 0 to 7 are PA4 to PA11.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="bus_write8">bus_Write8</h3>
<p>The lower 8-bits of arg1 are placed on the BUS, then, after a settling delay of approx 50nsec, the BUS_WR pin is strobed LO for approx 50nsec then set back HI.
The upper 8-bits of arg1 are ignored.</p>
<p><img alt="bus_Write8" src="../img/diablo16/bus_Write8.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>bus_Write8(value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The lower 8-bits of <strong>value</strong> are sent to the 8-bit bus.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-107-1" name="__codelineno-107-1" href="#__codelineno-107-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">data1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-107-2" name="__codelineno-107-2" href="#__codelineno-107-2"></a><span class="nl">data1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x05</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-107-3" name="__codelineno-107-3" href="#__codelineno-107-3"></a><span class="n">bus_Write8</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">data1</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="bus_setchangeinterrupt">bus_SetChangeInterrupt</h3>
<p>Any '1' bits in "portmask" marks that pin to generate an interrupt on change. A level change on that pin will cause "function" to be executed. If "function" is zero, the display may be put into sleep mode, and any change will cause a wakeup reset. Wakeup will always re-start code running in FLASHBANK_0 Bit 0 corresponds to PA0 through to bit15 which corresponds to PA15</p>
<p>Once armed, "function" will only be executed once, it is necessary to re-arm for any further events.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="qencoder1">Qencoder1</h3>
<p>Connect a quadrature encoder to a pair of pins, using the predefined 4D Pin Names in the table below, and the PHApin and PHBpin arguments in this function.</p>
<p>It is necessary to configure the pins first, depending on your requirements, e.g.</p>
<p><code>pin_Set(PIN_INP_HI, PA4); // PA4 as input, with pullup to Vcc</code></p>
<p>or maybe </p>
<p><code>pin_Set(PIN_INP, PA4); // PA4 as input, no pullup or pulldown</code></p>
<p>The position counter and delta can be read or written to at any time with peekW and pokeW using the following constants:</p>
<ul>
<li><code>QEN1_COUNTER_LO</code></li>
<li><code>QEN1_COUNTER_HI</code></li>
<li><code>QEN1_DELTA</code> (QEN1_DELTA is reset to 0 once it has been read.)</li>
</ul>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">4D Pin Name (Predefined)</th>

<h3 id="qencoder1reset">Qencoder1Reset</h3>
<p>Resets the Counters and Delta values for Encoder #1.</p>
<ul>
<li><code>QEN1_COUNTER_LO</code> is reset to zero.</li>
<li><code>QEN1_COUNTER_HI</code> is reset to zero.</li>
<li><code>QEN1_DELTA</code> is reset to zero.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>Qencoder1Reset();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-112-1" name="__codelineno-112-1" href="#__codelineno-112-1"></a><span class="n">Qencoder1Reset</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Reset the Counter and Delta values</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h3 id="pwm_init">pwm_Init</h3>
<p>This PWM function enables a PWM output on the desired pin, based on the availability set out by the table below.
Set the pin using the predefined 4D Pin Name into the pin argument, and select its mode and value, which are determined by:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">PWM Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_OFF</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Turn off the PWM (pin is left as Output)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_PLAIN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between <strong>0</strong> and <strong>1000</strong>. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is ~70kHz. A value of 1 is not valid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_SERVO</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Servo PWM has a value which is between <strong>100</strong> and <strong>200</strong>. This corresponds to 1.00 to 2.00ms. Please note values from 0 to 600 are valid (0-6ms) but should be used with caution. Repitition Rate is ~50Hz or 20ms.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWN_BINARY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Binary PWM which value is a number between <strong>0</strong> and <strong>1024</strong>. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is ~68kHz. A value of 1 is not valid.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_625HZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which corresponds to 62.5Hz, which takes a value from <strong>0</strong> to <strong>160</strong>.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_200HZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_500HZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_1KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_5KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_10KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_15KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_20KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_25KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_30KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PWM_35KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Plain PWM which value is a number between 0 and 1000. This corresponds to a 0.0 to 100.0% duty cycle. Raw Frequency is as specified.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>

<tbody>

<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">4D Pin Name to enable the PWM on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>

<h3 id="pin_pulseout">pin_Pulseout</h3>
<p>This function will invert the state of an output for "value" milliseconds.</p>
<p><strong>pin_Pulseout</strong> is a non-Blocking function, that is, code execution may continue while a pulse is occurring, and pulses can occur on multiple pins simultaneously.</p>
<p><strong>pin_PulseoutB</strong> is a Blocking function, where program execution is suspended during pulse.</p>
<p>If not already an output, pin is automatically made a push/pull output, and the last state of its output latch will determine pulse polarity.</p>
<p>Its open drain state is not altered if the pin was already an output.</p>
<p>If pulseout is called while pulseout is still active, the pulse timer will simply be updated with the new "value" and the pulse will continue with the extended value.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="pin_counter">pin_Counter</h3>
<p>Connect a counter to a pin to count transistions, and optionally call an event function when the 16bit counter wraps from 0xFFFF to zero.</p>
<p>The counter can be read or written to at any time with <a href="#peekw">peekW</a> and <a href="#pokew">pokeW</a>, therefore, the count may be set to 0xFFF0 for example, so that user function "<strong>OVFfuction</strong>" will be called after 16 pulses.</p>
<p>If "<strong>OVFfunction</strong>" is set to zero, only the counter will increment, and simply wrap back to zero from 0xFFFF. If "<strong>OVFfunction</strong>" points to a user function, wnen the event fires, <a href="#pin_counter">pin_Counter</a> will be disabled, and will need to be re-armed (ie '1shot' operation)</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="ana_hs">ana_HS</h3>
<p>Collects "samples" samples at "rate" frequency for 0 to 4 analogue pins and calls "userFunction" when done.</p>
<p>"rate" is samples represented as 1/100 samples per second, up to 250,000 reads/second across 1-4 channels. For example if you wish to sample at 5000 samples per second, you would set rate to be 50 as 5000 * 1/100 = 50.</p>
<p>Any unused IOx pins should have their buffer addresses (i.e. IO4buf) set to 0</p>
<p>For performance reasons samples are taken in chunks of 32, thus if you request 33 samples there will be a delay of 31 samples before "userFunction" is called</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>: <code>ana_HS(rate, samples, IO1buf, IO2buf, IO3buf, IO4buf, userFunction);</code></p>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">samples</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of samples to collect per analog channel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO1buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Buffer Address for first Analog Channel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OI2buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Buffer Address for second Analog Channel.</td>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO3buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Buffer Address for third Analog Channel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IO4buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Buffer Address for forth Analog Channel.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">userFunction</td>

</tr>
</tbody>

<h3 id="pin_pulseoutcount">pin_PulseoutCount</h3>
<p>This function will invert the state of an output at a "freq" freuency "count" times. This is a non-Blocking function, that is, code execution may continue while a pulse is occuring, and pulses can occur on multiple pins simultaneously. A function can be specified that will be called when all the pulses have been output. A maximum of 3 pulseoutCount activities can be active at any one point.</p>
<p>If not already an output, pin is automatically made a push/pull output, and the last state of its output latch will determine pulse polarity.</p>
<p>Its open drain state is not altered if the pin was already an output.</p>
<p>If pulseoutCount is called while pulseoutCount is active, the pulse counter will simply have the new count value added to it.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">4D Pin Name (Predefined)</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">DIABLO-16 Pin Number</th>
<th style="text-align: center;">Availability</th>
</tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="np_write">NP_Write</h3>
<p>Writes a string of pixels to the NeoPixel array connected to the specified I/O Pin.</p>
<p>Due to the critical timing requirements of the NeoPixel, any interrupts should be stopped, or otherwise <code>circumvented</code> before this command is issued. Internally, the system Timer is disabled during this command.</p>
<p>Comms Interrupts should also be disabled by the user, otherwise errors may occur. A suitable workaround is to repeat the NP_Write until <code>com_Count</code> does not change during its execution.</p>
<p>Comms TX Buffers, if used, should be held.</p>
<p>Audio should be stopped or paused.</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="graphics-functions">Graphics Functions</h2>
<h3 id="gfx_cls">gfx_Cls</h3>
<p>Clear the screen using the current background colour. <strong>gfx_Cls()</strong> command brings some of the settings back to default; such as,</p>
<ul>
<li>Transparency turned OFF</li>
<li>Outline colour set to BLACK</li>
<li>Opacity set to OPAQUE</li>
<li>Pen set to OUTLINE</li>
<li>Line patterns set to OFF</li>
<li>Right text margin set to full width</li>
<li>Text magnifications set to 1</li>
<li>All origins set to 0:0</li>
</ul>
<p>The alternative to maintain settings and clear screen is to draw a filled rectangle with the required background colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Cls();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-125-1" name="__codelineno-125-1" href="#__codelineno-125-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_BGcolour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">DARKGRAY</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-125-2" name="__codelineno-125-2" href="#__codelineno-125-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-125-3" name="__codelineno-125-3" href="#__codelineno-125-3"></a>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">newColour</td>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_circle">gfx_Circle</h3>
<p>Draws a circle with centre point x1, y1 with radius r using the specified colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Circle(x, y, rad, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x,y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the centre of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the radius of the circle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the circle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-127-1" name="__codelineno-127-1" href="#__codelineno-127-1"></a><span class="c1">// assuming PEN_SIZE is OUTLINE</span>
<a id="__codelineno-127-2" name="__codelineno-127-2" href="#__codelineno-127-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_Circle</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RED</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-127-3" name="__codelineno-127-3" href="#__codelineno-127-3"></a>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The default <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, however, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>SOLID</strong>, the circle will be drawn filled, if <strong>PEN_SIZE</strong> is set to <strong>OUTLINE</strong>, the circle will be drawn as an outline. If the circle is drawn as SOLID, the outline colour can be specified with <a href="#gfx_outlinecolour">gfx_OutlineColour(...)</a>. If <strong>OUTLINE_COLOUR</strong> is set to 0, no outline is drawn.</p>
</div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_roundrect">gfx_RoundRect</h3>
<p>Draw a filled rectangle at the given co-ordinates with optional rounded corners.</p>
<p>If x1 = x2 or y1 = y2 no straight line part is drawn.</p>
<p><img alt="gfx_RoundRect" src="../img/diablo16/gfx_RoundRect.png"></p>
<p>The actual width of the round-corners rectangle is computed by: <strong>2*rad + x2 – x1</strong>. <br>
The actual height of the round-corners rectangle is computed by: <strong>2*rad + y2 – y1</strong>.</p>
<p>Rendering can be obtained with <a href="#gfx_fillpattern">gfx_FillPattern(PATTRN)</a>; or gfx_FillPattern(OFF); for no fill pattern determined by <strong>‘radius’</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_RoundRect(x1, y1, x2, y2, rad, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the corner radius.This is the distance in pixels extending from the corners of the <strong>inner</strong> rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-134-1" name="__codelineno-134-1" href="#__codelineno-134-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">RoundRect</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RED</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="gfx_polyline">gfx_Polyline</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour. The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. gfx_Polyline can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p>This function is very similar to the <a href="#gfx_polygon">Polygon</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Polyline(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polyline.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the lines.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_polygon">gfx_Polygon</h3>
<p>Plots lines between points specified by a pair of arrays using the specified colour. The last point is drawn back to the first point, completing the polygon. The lines may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. gfx_Polygon can be used to create complex raster graphics by loading the arrays from serial input or from MEDIA with very little code requirement.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Polygon(n, vx, vy, colour);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">n</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of elements in the x and y arrays specifying the vertices for the polygon.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vx</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the x coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">vy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the addresses of the storage of the array of elements for the y coordinates of the vertices.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the polygon.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-136-1" name="__codelineno-136-1" href="#__codelineno-136-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vx</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">vy</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">7</span><span class="p">];</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_triangle">gfx_Triangle</h3>
<p>Draws a triangle outline between vertices x1,y1 , x2,y2 and x3,y3 using the specified colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function. Vertices must be specified in an anti-clockwise fashion.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Triangle(x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3, colour);</code></p>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the first vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the second vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x3, y3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the third vertices of the triangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour for the triangle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 id="gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit</h3>
<p>Sets up the internal pointers for the <a href="#gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit(..)</a> result variables. </tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y_dest</td>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_orbit">gfx_Orbit</h3>
<p>Sets Prior to using this function, the destination address of variables for the calculated coordinates must be set using the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(..)</a> function. The <strong>gfx_Orbit(..)</strong> function calculates the x, y coordinates of a distant point relative to the current origin, where the only known parameters are the <strong>angle</strong> and the <strong>distance</strong> from the current origin. The new coordinates are calculated and then placed in the destination variables that have been previously set with the <a href="#gfx_orbitinit">gfx_OrbitInit(..)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Orbit(angle, distance);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">angle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the angle from the origin to the remote point. The angle is specified in degrees.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">distance</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the distance from the origin to the remote point in pixel units.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-141-4" name="__codelineno-141-4" href="#__codelineno-141-4"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="gfx_getpixel">gfx_GetPixel</h3>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_GetPixel(x, y);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x,y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the screen coordinates of the pixel colour to be returned.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The 8 or 16bit colour of the pixel (default 16bit).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-143-1" name="__codelineno-143-1" href="#__codelineno-143-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_PutPixel</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-143-3" name="__codelineno-143-3" href="#__codelineno-143-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">r</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="gfx_incx">gfx_IncX</h3>
<p>Increment the current X origin by 1 pixel unit. The original value is returned before incrementing. The return value can be useful if a function requires the current point before insetting occurs.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_IncX();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The current X origin before the increment.</p>

<h3 id="gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</h3>
<p>Draws a line from the current origin to a new position. The Origin is then set to the new position. The line is drawn using the current object colour. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_LineTo(xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal position of the line end as well as the new origin.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical position of the line end as well as the new origin.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-148-1" name="__codelineno-148-1" href="#__codelineno-148-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_MoveTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-148-2" name="__codelineno-148-2" href="#__codelineno-148-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_LineTo</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">70</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-148-3" name="__codelineno-148-3" href="#__codelineno-148-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-148-4" name="__codelineno-148-4" href="#__codelineno-148-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example draws a line using the current object colour between x1=10,y1=20 and x2=60,y2=70. The new origin is now set at x=60,y=70.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</h3>
<p>Draws a line from the current origin to a new position. The line is drawn using the current object colour. The current origin is not altered. The line may be tessellated with the <a href="#gfx_linepattern">gfx_LinePattern(...)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_LineRel(xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_button">gfx_Button</h3>
<p>Draws a 3-dimensional Text Button at screen location defined by x, y parameters (top left corner). The size of the button depends on the font, width, height and length of the text. The button can contain multiple lines of text by having the <code>\n</code> character embedded in the string for the end of line marker. In this case, the widest text in the string sets the overall width, and the height of the button is set by the number of text lines. In the case of multiple lines, each line is left justified. If you wish to centre or right justify the text, you will need to prepare the text string according to your requirements.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Button(state, x, y, buttonColour, txtColour, font, txtWidth, txtHeight, text);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = Button pressed; 1 = Button raised.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the button on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buttonColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Button colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Text Colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">font</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the Font ID.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtWidth</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the text. This value is the font width multiplier and minimum value must be 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtHeight</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the text. This value is the font height multiplier and minimum value must be 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">text</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the text string. The text string must be within the range of printable ascii character set. The string may have <code>\n</code> characters embedded to create a multiline button.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_button3">gfx_Button3</h3>
<p>Draws a 3-dimensional Text Button at screen location defined by x, y parameters (top left corner). The size of the button is defined by the width and height parameters. The text is centred within those bounds. The button has <strong>rounded</strong> corners depending on <a href="#gfx_bevelradius">gfx_BevelRadius()</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Button3(mode, x, y, width, height, buttoncolour, textcolour, text);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = Button pressed; 1 = Button raised.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the button on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the button.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the button.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buttonColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Button colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">txtColour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Text Colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">text</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the text string. The text string must be within the range of printable ascii character set. The string may have \n characters embedded to create a multiline button.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the panel on the screen.</td>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_roundpanel">gfx_RoundPanel</h3>

</tr>

<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>

</tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_slider2">gfx_Slider2</h3>
<p>Draws a vertical or horizontal slider bar on the screen. The gfx_Slider function has several different modes of operation. In order to minimise the amount of graphics functions we need, all modes of operation are selected naturally depending on the parameter values.</p>
<p>Selection rules:</p>
<ol>
<li>If width &gt; height, slider is horizontal.</li>
<li>If height &lt;= width, slider is horizontal.</li>
<li>If value is positive, thumb is set to the position that is the proportion of value to the scale parameter.(used to set the control to the actual value of a variable)</li>
<li>If value is negative, thumb is driven to the graphics position set by the ABSolute of value. (used to set thumb to its actual graphical position (usually by touch screen)</li>
<li>The thumb colour is determine by <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(OBJECT_COLOUR, value);</a>, however, if the current object colour is BLACK, a darkened shade of the colour parameter is used for the thumb.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Slider2(mode, x1, y1, width, height, colour, scale, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">mode = 0 : Slider Indented, mode = 1 : Slider Raised, mode 2, Slider Hidden (background colour).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the height of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the Slider bar.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">scale</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">scale = n : sets the full scale range of the slider for the thumb from 0 to n.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">value = m : sets the relative position of the thumb 0 &lt;= m &lt;= n.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  If the value parameter was a positive number (i.e:- value is a proportion of the scale parameter), the true (implied x-axis or y-axis) position of the thumb is returned. <br>
If the value parameter was a negative number (i.e:- thumb is being set to an ABSolute graphics position), the actual slider value (which is a proportion of the scale parameter) is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_screencopypaste">gfx_ScreenCopyPaste</h3>
<p>Copies an area of a screen from xs, ys of size given by width and height parameters and pastes it to another location determined by xd, yd.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ScreenCopyPaste(xs, ys, xd, yd, width, height);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xs, ys</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the area to be copied (source).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xd, yd</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of where the paste is to be made (destination).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the width of the copied area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">height</td>

</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_slider">gfx_Slider</h3>
<p>Draws a vertical or horizontal slider bar on the screen. The gfx_Slider function has several different modes of operation. In order to minimise the amount of graphics functions we need, all modes of operation are selected naturally depending on the parameter values.</p>
<p>Selection rules:</p>
<ol>
<li>If x2-x1 &gt; y2-y1 slider is assumed to be horizontal (ie: if width &gt; height, slider is horizontal).</li>
<li>If x2-x1 &lt;= y2-y1 slider is assumed to be vertical (ie: if height &lt;= width, slider is horizontal).</li>
<li>If value is positive, thumb is set to the position that is the proportion of value to the scale parameter.(used to set the control to the actual value of a variable).</li>
<li>If value is negative, thumb is driven to the graphics position set by the ABSolute of value. (used to set thumb to its actual graphical position (usually by touch screen).</li>
<li>The thumb colour is determine by <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(OBJECT_COLOUR, value);</a>, however, if the current object colour is BLACK, a darkened shade of the colour parameter is used for the thumb.</li>
</ol>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Slider(mode, x1, y1, x2, y2, colour, scale, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">mode = 0 : Slider Indented, mode = 1 : Slider Raised, mode 2, Slider Hidden (background colour).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner position of the slider on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the colour of the Slider bar.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">scale</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">scale = n : sets the full scale range of the slider for the thumb from 0 to n.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">if value positive, sets the relative position of the thumb on the slider bar, else set thumb to ABS position of the negative number.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  If the value parameter was a positive number (i.e:- value is a proportion of the scale parameter), the true (implied x-axis or y-axis) position of the thumb is returned. <br>
If the value parameter was a negative number (i.e:- thumb is being set to an ABSolute graphics position), the actual slider value (which is a proportion of the scale parameter) is returned.</p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-160-1" name="__codelineno-160-1" href="#__codelineno-160-1"></a><span class="n">func</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="nf">drawRedSlider</span><span class="p">()</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_origin">gfx_Origin</h3>
<p>Sets relative screen offset for horizontal and vertical for the top left corner for graphics objects.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Origin(x, y);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-166-1" name="__codelineno-166-1" href="#__codelineno-166-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_Origin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Sets origin position at (10, 20)</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_get">gfx_Get</h3>
<p>Returns various graphics parameters to caller.</p>
<p>The following graphics parameters can be queried:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>X_MAX</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Current orientations Max X Value (X_MAX)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>Y_MAX</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Current orientations Max Y Value (Y_MAX)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>LEFT_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Left location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>TOP_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>RIGHT_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Right location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>BOTTOM_POS</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom location of Object</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>X_ORG</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Get current internal X position</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;"><code>Y_ORG</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Get current internal Y position</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Get(mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies graphics parameter to query.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  </p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Mode</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the maximum horizontal value of the display.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the maximum vertical value of the display.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the left location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the top location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the right location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the bottom location of the last drawn object such as a slider or button or an image/video.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the internal X position that was set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(x, y)</a>; or <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(X_ORG, pos)</a>;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Returns the internal Y position that was set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(x, y)</a>; or <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(X_ORG, pos)</a>;</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow</h3>
<p>Specifies a clipping window region on the screen such that any objects and text placed onto the screen will be clipped and displayed only within that region. For the clipping window to take effect, "Clipping" setting must be enabled separately using <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Set(CLIPPING, ON)</a> or the shortcut <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_Clipping(ON)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ClipWindow(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the top left corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal and vertical position of the bottom right corner of the clipping window.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-168-1" name="__codelineno-168-1" href="#__codelineno-168-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-168-2" name="__codelineno-168-2" href="#__codelineno-168-2"></a><span class="n">gfx_ClipWindow</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-168-3" name="__codelineno-168-3" href="#__codelineno-168-3"></a><span class="nl">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">50000</span><span class="p">;</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_set">gfx_Set</h3>
<p>Given a function number and a value, set the required graphics control parameter, such as size, colour, and other parameters. (See the <strong>Single parameter short-cuts for the gfx_Set functions</strong> below). It is strongly recommended to use the pre-defined constants rather than the mode numbers.</p>
<p>Single parameter short-cuts for the gfx_Set functions</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">PEN_SIZE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the draw mode for <a href="#gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</a>, <a href="#gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</a>, <a href="#gfx_dot">gfx_Dot</a>, <a href="#gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</a> and <a href="#gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</a> (default mode is <strong>OUTLINE</strong>)*</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>SOLID</strong> <br>1 or <strong>OUTLINE</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">BACKGROUND_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set the screen background colour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0-65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OBJECT_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Generic colour for <a href="#gfx_lineto">gfx_LineTo</a>, <a href="#gfx_linerel">gfx_LineRel</a>, <a href="#gfx_dot">gfx_Dot</a>, <a href="#gfx_bullet">gfx_Bullet</a> and <a href="#gfx_boxto">gfx_BoxTo</a></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0-65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">CLIPPING</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Turns clipping on/off. <br>The clipping points are set with <a href="#gfx_clipwindow">gfx_ClipWindow</a> and must be set first.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 or 0 (<strong>ON</strong> or <strong>OFF</strong>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TRANSPARENT_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour that needs to be made transparent.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0-65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TRANSPARENCY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Turn the transparency ON or OFF. Transparency is automatically turned OFF after the next image or video command.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1 or 0 (<strong>ON</strong> or <strong>OFF</strong>)</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">FRAME_DELAY</td>

<td style="text-align: left;">0 to 255msec</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">SCREEN_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set required screen behaviour/orientation.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>LANDSCAPE</strong> <br>1 or <strong>LANDSCAPE_R</strong> <br>2 or <strong>PORTRAIT</strong> <br>3 or <strong>PORTRAIT_R</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OUTLINE_COLOUR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outline colour for rectangles and circles(set to 0 for no effect)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour, 0-65535</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">CONTRAST</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>LCD MODULES:</strong> <br> contrast 0 = display OFF, 1-15 = contrast level (Actually backlight brightness)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>OFF</strong> <br>1 to 15 for levels</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LINE_PATTERN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the line draw pattern for line drawing. If set to zero, lines are solid, else each '1' bit represents a pixel that is turned off. <br> Example: <br><code>gfx_Set(LINE_PATTERN, 0b1111000011110000); // draw dotted line</code></td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>OFF</strong> <br>1 to 0xFFFF <br>0 bits for pixels on <br>1 bits for pixels off</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COLOUR_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets 8 or 16bit colour mode. <br>Function not available, fixed as 16bit mode.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 or <strong>COLOUR16</strong> <br>1 or <strong>COLOUR8</strong></td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">BEVEL_WIDTH</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Set Button Bevel Width, 0 pixel to 15pixels.</td>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Although it is often required to be able to set graphics functions with a single function call for graphics engine related functions, there is a complete set of single parameter shortcut functions that have exactly the same function as each of the gfx_Set modes and saves 1 parameter, i.e. uses less memory.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_arc">gfx_Arc</h3>
<p>Draws an arc at "xc":"yc" with radius "radius", starting at "startangle" and ending at "endangle". Colour is determined by current object colour.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Arc(cx, cy, radius, step, startangle, endangle, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">cx, cy</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Center of the arc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">radius</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Radius of the arc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">step</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Step is the stepping angle increment for the fineness of the arc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">startangle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Starting angle of the arc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">endangle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Ending angle of the arc.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">mode = 0, outer circumference line only. <br>mode = 1, outer circumference and lines back to cx:cy.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_fillpattern">gfx_FillPattern</h3>
<p>Selects a tessellating pattern for painting solid objects. <strong>‘patptr’</strong> points to a 8x8 tile for rendering filled areas.
Rendering is turned off with <strong>gfx_FillPattern(0, mode);</strong> or <strong>gfx_FillPattern(OFF, mode);</strong></p>
<p><strong>‘mode’</strong> maybe TRANSPARENT or OPAQUE (0 or 1), for OPAQUE mode, the current screen colour is used for the 'off' pixels, for transparent mode, the 'off' pixels are not drawn.</p>
<p><strong>gfx_FillPattern</strong> affects all filled object, including polygons. There are 32 builtin patterns; these are obtained using the pre-defined constants <strong>FILLPATTERN_0</strong> to <strong>FILLPATTERN_31</strong>. Note that the constants range from 0xFFE0 to 0xFFFF, any other value is assumed to be a pointer to a user’s 8 byte block pattern.
Predefined constants are used to select the internal patterns, <strong>FILLPATTERN_0</strong> through to <strong>FILLPATTERN_31</strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_FillPattern(patptr, mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">patptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0 = 0ff, 0xFFE0 to 0xFFFF = builtin patterns, else patptr points to a users 8 byte pattern.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">TRANSPARENT or OPAQUE (0 or 1)</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The handle of the previous pattern.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-172-1" name="__codelineno-172-1" href="#__codelineno-172-1"></a><span class="n">gfx_FillPattern</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">OFF</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">TRANSPARENT</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Turns OFF pattern rendering</span>
<a id="__codelineno-172-2" name="__codelineno-172-2" href="#__codelineno-172-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-172-3" name="__codelineno-172-3" href="#__codelineno-172-3"></a><span class="n">gfx_FillPattern</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FILLPATTERN_31</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">TRANSPARENT</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-172-4" name="__codelineno-172-4" href="#__codelineno-172-4"></a><span class="c1">// Renders FILLPATTERN_31 in transparent mode for filled objects</span>
<a id="__codelineno-172-5" name="__codelineno-172-5" href="#__codelineno-172-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-172-6" name="__codelineno-172-6" href="#__codelineno-172-6"></a><span class="n">gfx_FillPattern</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">FILLPATTERN_17</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OPAQUE</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-172-7" name="__codelineno-172-7" href="#__codelineno-172-7"></a><span class="c1">// Renders FILLPATTERN_17 in OPAQUE mode for filled objects</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_gradient">gfx_Gradient</h3>
<p>Draws a graduated colour rectangle at the specified co-ordinate.
Rendering can be obtained with <a href="#gfx_fillpattern">gfx_FillPattern(PATTRN)</a>; or <a href="#gfx_fillpattern">gfx_FillPattern(OFF)</a>; for no fill pattern.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Gradient(style, x1, y1, x2, y2, color1, color2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">style</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies gradient style. <br>GRAD_DOWN gradient changes in the vertical direction <br>GRAD_RIGHT gradient change in the horizontal direction <br>GRAD_UP gradient changes in the vertical direction <br>GRAD_LEFT gradient change in the horizontal direction <br>GRAD_WAVE_VER gradient wave in the vertical direction <br>GRAD_WAVE_HOR gradient wave in the horizontal direction</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies top left corner of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies bottom right corner of the rectangle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">color1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies starting colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">color2</td>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_readbresline">gfx_readBresLine</h3>
<p>Due to the fact that most LCDs are not double buffered, and memory is limited on small platforms, <strong>gfx_ReadBresLine</strong> offers a simple but powerful way of manipulating raster lines by storing all the pixels for an arbitrary line.</p>
<p>Typically, <strong>gfx_ReadBresLine</strong> is used when ‘rubber banding’ a rectangular area when dragging a marker rectangle, or drawing a needle on a pre-rendered meter or gauge image. The power of this function is further extended when used with the array math functions.</p>
<p><strong>gfx_ReadBresLine</strong> reads an arbitrary line from the display to an array.
If "ptr" is 0, the correctly sized array is created, in which case it is up to the caller to eventually destroy it when no longer required. Otherwise, "ptr" is expected to point to a correctly sized array.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_readBresLine(x1, y1, x2, y2, ptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Line mapping start point.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Line mapping end point.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">If zero is passed, an array of the required size to map the line is created. If non zero, it is expected that this is a pointer to an array large enough to store each pixel that is read.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the created array, or the users array. In the case of ptr=0 (creation of array), if there is insufficient memory to create the array, zero is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-178-1" name="__codelineno-178-1" href="#__codelineno-178-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-2" name="__codelineno-178-2" href="#__codelineno-178-2"></a><span class="nl">array</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">gfx_ReadBresLine</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">50</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">250</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">175</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-3" name="__codelineno-178-3" href="#__codelineno-178-3"></a><span class="c1">// Copy the pixels of the line with endpoint at (50,50) and (250, 175)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-4" name="__codelineno-178-4" href="#__codelineno-178-4"></a><span class="c1">// and saves it to the generated array. The address is then returned</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-5" name="__codelineno-178-5" href="#__codelineno-178-5"></a><span class="c1">// and saved to the variable 'array'</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-6" name="__codelineno-178-6" href="#__codelineno-178-6"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-178-7" name="__codelineno-178-7" href="#__codelineno-178-7"></a><span class="n">gfx_BGcolour</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">LIME</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-8" name="__codelineno-178-8" href="#__codelineno-178-8"></a><span class="n">gfx_Cls</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Sets the background to a single color</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-9" name="__codelineno-178-9" href="#__codelineno-178-9"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-178-10" name="__codelineno-178-10" href="#__codelineno-178-10"></a><span class="n">gfx_WriteBresLine</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">225</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-11" name="__codelineno-178-11" href="#__codelineno-178-11"></a><span class="c1">// Copies the line to the new</span>
<a id="__codelineno-178-12" name="__codelineno-178-12" href="#__codelineno-178-12"></a><span class="c1">// Endpoints are at (100,100) and (300,225)</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If an array is supplied, its size must be large enough, and may be calculated:</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_readgramarea">gfx_ReadGRAMarea</h3>
<p>Reads an arbitrary rectangular area from the display to an array. If "ptr" is 0, the correctly sized array is created, in which case it is up to the caller to eventually destroy it. Otherwise, "ptr" is expected to point to a correctly sized array.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_ReadGRAMarea(x1, y1, x2, y2, ptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left corner of the rectangular area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom right corner of the rectangular area.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">If zero is passed, an array of the required size to map the line is created. If non zero, it is expected that this is a pointer to an array large enough to store each pixel that is read.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the created aray, or the users array. In the case of ptr=0, if there is insufficient memory to create the array, zero is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-180-1" name="__codelineno-180-1" href="#__codelineno-180-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">array</span><span class="p">;</span>

<h3 id="gfx_surround">gfx_Surround</h3>
<p>Draws an outline rectangle at the given co-ordinates with optional rounded corners determined by <strong>‘rad1’</strong>.
<strong>‘rad2’</strong> is added to <strong>‘rad1’</strong> to form the outer rounded rectangle.
If <strong>‘rad1’</strong> is zero, the inner rectangle will have square corners.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Surround(x1, y1, x2, y2, rad1, rad2, color);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
