<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1, y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left corner position of the surround on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2, y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the bottom right corner position of the surround on the screen.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Inner corner radius.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rad2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer corner radius.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">color</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The colour of the surround.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_scope">gfx_Scope</h3>
<p>Draws up to 4 waveforms from table(s) of vertices at the specified origin. Also useful for drawing line graphs.</p>
<p>X position is incremented each point by "Xstep" pixels. Values are skipped for negative values. Y values are derived from a Y buffer. <br>
After the waveform is drawn, "newy" buffer is automatically copied to "oldy" buffer. Use 0 as the buffers for any unused waveforms.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Scope(left, width, Yzero, N, Xstep, Yamp, colourbg, old_y1, new_y1, colour1, old_y2, new_y2, colour2, old_y3, new_y3, colour3, old_y4, new_y4, colour4);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">left</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The left margin of the Scope.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">width</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The width of the Scope.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Yzero</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The y position that corresponds to a y value of zero, normally "Top" + "Height" for a graph, or "Top" + "Height"/2 for a scope.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">N</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The number of elements in each buffer. This will need to be greater than "width" for negative "Xstep" values.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Xstep</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">X position is incremented each point by "xstep" pixels.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Yamp</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Amplification in the Y direction, 100 is unity.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colourbg</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The color of the Scope’s Background.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">oldy1..4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Buffer containing most recent set of points to be un-drawn.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">newy1..4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Buffer containing new points to be drawn.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">colour1..4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Colour of the waveform.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_panel2">gfx_Panel2</h3>
<p>Draws a panel2 (groupbox) at screen location defined by x, y, width and height with left colour "cl" and right colour "cr"and option fill colour "cf".</p>
<p>w1 and w2 define the width of the outer and inner borders.</p>
<p>state = 0 : recessed <br>
state = 1 : raised <br>
state + PANEL2_FILLED : draws with fill color "cf"</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_Panel2(state, x, y, width, height, w1, w2, cl, cr, cf);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>For optimal appearance, calculate number of bars for given height first using this formula: </p>
<p><code>bars = ( (gauge height / 2) + (spacing / 2) + 1) / ( (bar thickness / 2) + (spacing / 2) + 2)</code> </p>
<p>then calculate exact height given the calculated ticks: </p>
<p><code>height = bars * ( (bar thickness / 2) + (spacing / 2) +2) – (spacing / 2) - 1</code></p>
</div>

<h3 id="gfx_leddigit">gfx_LedDigit</h3>
<p>Draws a single 7 segment led Digit at x, y of size digitsize using oncolour and offcolour. The value can be 0-9 (0-9), A-F (0x0a-0x0f), blank(0x10) and - (0x11). Or value with LEDDIGIT_F_SHOW_DP to show a decimal point, LEDDIGIT_F_DP_COMMA to make the Decimal point a comma and LEDDIGIT_F_DP_ON to turn the decimal point on LEDDIGIT_F_SET_SEGMENTS can be used to turn value into a series of bits to turn on individual segments e.g. LEDDIGIT_F_SET_SEGMENTS + 9 will turn on the top and bottom segments. Again LEDDIGIT_F_SHOW_DP and LEDDIGIT_F_DP_COMMA can be used, but in this case the DP is the 8th segment.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_LedDigit(x, y, digitsize, oncolour, offcolour, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">x- and y-coordinates of position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">digitsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Size of digit.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">oncolour</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Color when status is on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">offcolour</td>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_gradientshape">gfx_GradientShape</h3>
<p>Produce a shaped color gradient using the supplied parameters.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>gfx_GradientShape(GradientRAM, HorzVert, OuterWidth, X, Y, W, H, TLrad, TRrad, BLrad, BRrad, Darken, OuterColor, OuterType, OuterLevel, InnerColor, InnerType, InnerLevel, Split);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">GradientRAM</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">This Function requires a quantity or RAM to work. It also needs to be initialised and it's size varies accoring to the largest corner radius. Multiple gradient shape calls can share the same GradientRAM. egr gradientRAM[29+91*2] := [-1,-1,-9999,0,0,91] ; Would support a maximum radius of 90 degrees, note the 91 in two places.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HorzVert</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Horizontal or Vertical -- 0 or 1.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OuterWidth</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer gradient width.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">X</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">x co-ordinate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">y co-ordinate.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">W</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Width</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">H</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Height</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TLrad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left corner radius.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">TRrad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top right corner radius.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">BLrad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom left radius.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">BRrad</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Bottom right radius.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Darken</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Darken both colours by a value. Can be a -ve value to lighten.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OuterColor</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer Gradient colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OuterType</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer Gradient type (0 - 3 horizontal, +4 vertical) <br>0 - Raised <br>1 - Sunken <br>2 - Raised flatter middle <br>3 - Sunken flatter middle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OuterLevel</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer Gradient level 0 - 63.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">InnerColor</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Inner Gradient colour.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">InnerType</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Outer Gradient type (0 - 3 horizontal, +4 vertical) <br>0 - Raised <br>1 - Sunken <br>2 - Raised flatter middle <br>3 - Sunken flatter middle</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">InnerLevel</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Inner Gradient level 0 - 63.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Split</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Split gradient. <br>0 - no split <br>1 – top <br>2 - bottom</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<a id="__codelineno-217-2" name="__codelineno-217-2" href="#__codelineno-217-2"></a><span class="w">                    </span><span class="n">TRrad</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BLrad</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">BRrad</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Darken</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OuterColor</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OuterType</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OuterLevel</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">InnerColor</span><span class="p">,</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="gfx_xyrottoval">gfx_XYrotToVal</h3>

<td style="text-align: left;">Relative y-coordinate (y-coordinate – y-center).</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<h2 class="page-break" id="i2c-master-functions">I2C Master Functions</h2>
<h3 id="i2c_open">I2C_Open</h3>
<p>Calling this function configures the I2C module and initialises it to be ready for service. The I2C clock speed is specified by the Speed parameter. Multiple I2C Speed settings are available to suit various requirements.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Speed</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_SLOW</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">100KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_MED</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">400KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_FAST</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1MHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_10KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">10KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_20KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">20KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_50KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">50KHz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C_250KHZ</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">250KHz</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Open(Speed, SCLpin, SDApin);</code> or <code>I2C2_Open(Speed, SCLpin, SDApin);</code> or <code>I2C3_Open(Speed, SCLpin, SDApin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the I2C bus speed (See the table above).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">SCLpin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the GPIO pin to use for the SCL signal.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">SDApin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the GPIO pin to use for the SDA signal.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if Successful, otherwise 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-222-1" name="__codelineno-222-1" href="#__codelineno-222-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Open</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">I2C_MED</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA3</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Open the I2C port in 400KHz mode.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Normally the I2C pins are PA0 to PA13, use of these pins has a couple of limitations, a) There is no slew rate control at I2C_MED and b) I2C_FAST is not truly 1MHz. If either of these restrictions need to be addressed, a special case of SCLpin = PA14 and SDApin = PA15 exists ONLY for speeds I2C_MED (which uses slew rate control) and I2C_FAST (which is truly 1MHz).</p>
</div>
<h3 id="i2c_close">I2C_Close</h3>
<p>Calling this function closes the I2C port and disables the I2C hardware</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Close();</code> or <code>I2C2_Close();</code> or <code>I2C3_Close();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-223-1" name="__codelineno-223-1" href="#__codelineno-223-1"></a><span class="n">I2C3_Close</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Close I2C port and Disable the hardware</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2c_start">I2C_Start</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C start condition.
The hardware first pulls the SDA (data) line low, and next pulls the SCL (clock) line low.</p>
<p><img alt="I2C_Start" src="../img/diablo16/I2C_Start.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Start();</code> or <code>I2C2_Start();</code> or <code>I2C3_start();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if Successful, otherwise 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-224-1" name="__codelineno-224-1" href="#__codelineno-224-1"></a><span class="n">I2C2_Start</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Send an I2C start condition.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_stop">I2C_Stop</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C stop condition. The hardware first releases the SCL to high state, and then releases the SDA line high.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_stop" src="../img/diablo16/I2C_Stop.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Stop();</code> or <code>I2C2_Stop();</code> or <code>I2C3_Stop();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if Successful, otherwise 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-225-1" name="__codelineno-225-1" href="#__codelineno-225-1"></a><span class="n">I2C1_Stop</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Send</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Stop</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="i2c_restart">I2C_Restart</h3>
<p>Calling this function generates a restart condition.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Restart();</code> or <code>I2C2_Restart();</code> or <code>I2C3_Restart();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if Successful, otherwise 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-226-1" name="__codelineno-226-1" href="#__codelineno-226-1"></a><span class="n">I2C3_Restart</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Generates an I2C restart condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_read">I2C_Read</h3>
<p>Calling this function reads a single byte from the I2C bus.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_read" src="../img/diablo16/i2c_read.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Read();</code> or <code>I2C2_Read();</code> or <code>I2C3_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Byte from the I2C Bus in the lower 8-bits.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-227-1" name="__codelineno-227-1" href="#__codelineno-227-1"></a><span class="nl">ch</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C1_Read</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Read a single byte from the I2C Bus.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Data can only change when the clock is low.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_write">I2C_Write</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends a single byte to the I2C bus</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_write" src="../img/diablo16/i2c_write.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Write(byte);</code> or <code>I2C2_Write(byte);</code> or <code>I2C3_Write(byte);</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The byte to be written to the I2C Bus.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-228-1" name="__codelineno-228-1" href="#__codelineno-228-1"></a><span class="nl">Status</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C3_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">bytevalue</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send a single byte to the I2C Bus.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_ack">I2C_Ack</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C acknowledge condition. The hardware first pulls the SDA line low, and next releases SCL high followed by pulling SCL low again thus generating a clock pulse, SDA is then released high.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_ack" src="../img/diablo16/i2c_ack.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Ack();</code> or <code>I2C2_Ack();</code> or <code>I2C3_Ack();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-229-1" name="__codelineno-229-1" href="#__codelineno-229-1"></a><span class="n">I2C2_Ack</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Send I2C Acknowledge condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Data can only change when the clock is low.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_nack">I2C_Nack</h3>
<p>Calling this function sends an I2C negative acknowledge condition. The hardware first release the SDA line high, and next releases SCL HI followed by pulling SCL low thus generating a clock pulse.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_nak" src="../img/diablo16/I2c_nak.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Nack();</code> or <code>I2C2_Nack();</code> or <code>I2C3_Nack();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-230-1" name="__codelineno-230-1" href="#__codelineno-230-1"></a><span class="n">I2C3_Nack</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Send an I2C Negative acknowledge condition</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Data can only change when the clock is low.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_ackstatus">I2C_AckStatus</h3>
<p>Call this function to get the ACK status from the slave device
The state of SDA is returned.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_ackstatus" src="../img/diablo16/i2c_ackstatus.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_AckStatus();</code> or <code>I2C2_AckStatus();</code> or <code>I2C3_AckStatus();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Device Ack Status.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-231-1" name="__codelineno-231-1" href="#__codelineno-231-1"></a><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C1_AckStatus</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// returns the Ack</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Returns the state of SDA after the last clock pulse.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_ackpoll">I2C_AckPoll</h3>
<p>Call this function to wait for a device to return an ACK during ACK polling.
The SDA is monitored for an Ack.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_ackpoll" src="../img/diablo16/i2c_ackpoll.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_AckPoll();</code> or <code>I2C2_AckPoll();</code> or <code>I2C3_AckPoll();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Device Ack Status.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-232-1" name="__codelineno-232-1" href="#__codelineno-232-1"></a><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C2_AckPoll</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0xA0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">//send the control byte the wait for a device</span>
<a id="__codelineno-232-2" name="__codelineno-232-2" href="#__codelineno-232-2"></a><span class="w">                            </span><span class="c1">//to return poll the device until an ACK</span>
<a id="__codelineno-232-3" name="__codelineno-232-3" href="#__codelineno-232-3"></a><span class="w">                            </span><span class="c1">//is received.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Returns the state of SDA after the last clock pulse.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="i2c_idle">I2C_Idle</h3>
<p>Call this function to wait until the I2C bus is inactive.</p>
<p><img alt="i2c_idle" src="../img/diablo16/i2c_idle.png"></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>I2C1_Idle();</code> or <code>I2C2_Idle();</code> or <code>I2C2_Idle();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if Successful, otherwise 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-233-1" name="__codelineno-233-1" href="#__codelineno-233-1"></a><span class="nl">r</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">I2C1_Idle</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//Wait until the I2C Bus is inactive.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Wait for the bus to become idle. Times out if not inactive within 1 second.</p>
</div>

<h2 class="page-break" id="image-control-functions">Image Control Functions</h2>
<h3 id="img_setposition">img_SetPosition</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>; function.</p>
<p>Sets the position where the image will next be displayed. Returns TRUE if index was ok and function was successful. (the return value is usually ignored).</p>
<p>You may turn off an image so when <a href="#img_show">img_Show()</a> is called, the image will not be shown.</p>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a>; function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_SetPosition(handle, index, xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left horizontal screen position where image is to be displayed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Top left vertical screen position where image is to be displayed.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if index OK, otherwise false.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-238-1" name="__codelineno-238-1" href="#__codelineno-238-1"></a><span class="c1">// make a simple 'window'</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="img_enable">img_Enable</h3>

</tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_setword">img_SetWord</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...);</a> function.

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMAGE_XPOS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">WORD image location X</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">IMAGE_YPOS</td>
<td style="text-align: center;">3</td>

e.g.:- img_ClearAttributes(hndl, ALL, I_Y_LOCK | I_X_LOCK ); // allow all images to move in any direction.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_touched">img_Touched</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function.</p>
<p>Returns index if image touched or returns -1 image not touched.
If index is passed as -1 the function tests all images and returns -1 if image not touched or returns index.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_Touched(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_selectreadposition">img_SelectReadPosition</h3>
<p>This Functions sets a position in an image control for sequential reading of pixels from the uSD card (fat16 or raw modes supported).</p>
<p>No image window area is set, the image will not be shown.</p>
<p>This function provides a means of preparing to load an image, or part of an image, to an array. (see img_SequentialRead)</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_SelectReadPosition(handle, index, frame, xpos, ypos);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the Image List.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the images in the list.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">frame</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Frame to read if the ‘image’ is a video, else 0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Image location, x position (top left corner).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Image location, Y position (top left corner).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if index was ok and function successful.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_sequentialread">img_SequentialRead</h3>
<p>Once a position has been set with the <a href="#img_selectreadposition">img_SelectReadPosition</a> function, this function can then be used for sequential reading of pixels from image storage.</p>
<p>If "ptr" is 0, "count" pixels from the stream are simply skipped.</p>
<p>If "ptr" is 1, "count" pixels are written to the GRAM area.</p>
<p>"ptr" must point to a valid array that is at least the size of "count", or part of an image, to an array. (see <a href="#img_selectreadposition">img_SelectReadPosition</a>)</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_SequentialRead(count, ptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of Pixels to read.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A pointer to an array to read count pixels into.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if index was ok and function successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See <a href="#img_selectreadposition">img_SelectReadPosition</a> example</p>
<h3 id="img_fileread">img_FileRead</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Reads the number of bytes specified by "<strong>size</strong>" from the file referenced by "<strong>handle</strong>" into a destination memory buffer. If "<strong>dest</strong>" is zero, data is directed to GRAM window.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FileRead(*dest, size, handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>

<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to a destination memory buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to be read.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileseek">img_FileSeek</h3>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_filetell">img_FileTell</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Reads the current 32-bit file pointer and stores it into the two variables specified in "<strong>HiWord</strong>" and "<strong>LoWord</strong>".</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FileTell(handle, index, &amp;HiWord, &amp;LoWord);</code></p>

</tr>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_filegets">img_FileGetS</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>This function reads a line of text to a buffer (specified by "<strong>*string</strong>") from a file at the current file position indicated by the associated file-position pointer and advances the pointer appropriately.</p>
<p>This function reads only reads up to "<strong>size - 1</strong>" characters into "<strong><em>string</em>*" (one character is reserved for the null-terminator). Characters are read until either a newline or an EOF is received or until the number of characters read reaches "</strong>size - 1**" or a read error is received.</p>
<p><a href="#img_filegets">img_FileGetS(...)</a> automatically appends a null-terminator to the data read.</p>
<p><a href="#img_filegets">img_FileGetS(...)</a> will stop reading when any of the following conditions are true:</p>
<ul>
<li>It has read n-1 bytes (one character is reserved for the null-terminator).</li>
<li>It encounters a newline character (a line-feed in the compilers tested here), or</li>
<li>It reaches the end of file.</li>
<li>A read error occurs.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FileGetS(*string, size, handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The maximum number of bytes to be read from the file.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to string or null if failed.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-257-1" name="__codelineno-257-1" href="#__codelineno-257-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileGets</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystr</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">81</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hnd1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// read up to 80 chars</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</p>
</div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileloadfunction">img_FileLoadFunction</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Load a function or program from disk and return a function pointer to the allocation.</p>
<p>The function can then be invoked just like any other function would be called via a function pointer.
Parameters may be passed to it in a conventional way. The callers stack is shared by the loaded function, however any global variables in the loaded function are private to that function.</p>
<p>The function may be discarded at any time when no longer required, freeing its memory resources through <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(..)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FileLoadFunction( handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the memory allocation where the function has been loaded from file which can be then used as a function call.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_filerun">img_FileRun</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Load a program from disk where the current program releases any allocated memory but retains the stack and global memory.</p>
<p>If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else, arglist points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array.</p>
<p>The func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any. The arguments can only be passed by value, no pointers or references can be used as all memory is cleared before the file is loaded.</p>
<p>Refer to <a href="#img_fileexec">img_FileExec(...)</a> and <a href="#img_fileloadfunction">img_FileLoadFunction(…)</a> for functions that can pass by reference.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FileRun(handle, index, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-262-1" name="__codelineno-262-1" href="#__codelineno-262-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileRun</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">index</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">argptr</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileexec">img_FileExec</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Load a program from disk and returns like a function, the calling program is kept active and control returns to it.</p>
<p>The func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any. If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else arglist points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array</p>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#img_fileloadfunction">img_FileLoadFunction(...)</a>, however, the function argument list is passed by pointer, and the memory consumed by the function is released as soon as the function completes.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FileExec(handle, index, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-263-1" name="__codelineno-263-1" href="#__codelineno-263-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">img_FileExec</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">hndl</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">index</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">argptr</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function is only for files embedded in a GCF, for Flash only, ie this is not valid for GCI and uSD card access.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="img_fileplaywav">img_FilePlayWAV</h3>
<p>This function requires that an image file control has been created with the <a href="#file_loadimagecontrol">file_LoadImageControl(...)</a> function under <strong>Mode 3</strong>.</p>
<p>Play a wave file at index "<strong>index</strong>" in the image filesystem "<strong>handle</strong>". This function automatically grabs a chunk of memory for a file buffer, and a wave buffer.</p>
<p>The minimum memory requirement is about 580 bytes for the disk I/O service and a minimum wave buffer size of 1024. The size of the wave buffer allocation can be increased by the snd_BufSize function. The default size 1024 bytes. The memory is only required during the duration of play, and is automatically released while not in use.</p>
<p>See <a href="#sound-control-functions"><strong>Sound Control Functions</strong></a> for additional play control functions.</p>
<p id="img_fileplayway_errors">This function may return the following error values:</p>

<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Insufficient memory available for WAV buffer and file</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">cant play this rate</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no data chunk found in first rsector</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no format data</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">no wave chunk signature</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">bad wave file format</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">-1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">file not found</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>img_FilePlayWAV(handle, index);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">handle</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the image file control.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">index</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Index of the entry in the handle.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of blocks to play (1 to 32767) or negative value in case of <a href="#img_fileplayway_errors">errors</a></p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="rand">RAND</h3>
<p>This function returns a pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767.</p>
<p>The random number generator may first be seeded by using the SEED(number) function. The seed will generate a pseudo random sequence that is repeatable. You can use the modulo operator (%) to return a number within a certain range, e.g. n := RAND() % 100; will return a random number between -99 and +99. If you are using random number generation for random graphics points, or only require a positive number set, you will need to use the ABS function so only a positive number is returned, e.g.: X1 := ABS(RAND() % 100); will set co-ordinate X1 between 0 and 99.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>RAND();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pseudo random signed number ranging from -32768 to +32767 each time the function is called.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-272-1" name="__codelineno-272-1" href="#__codelineno-272-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-2" name="__codelineno-272-2" href="#__codelineno-272-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-272-3" name="__codelineno-272-3" href="#__codelineno-272-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-272-4" name="__codelineno-272-4" href="#__codelineno-272-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print **3558**, **1960** to the display.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>that if the random number generator is not seeded, the first number returned after reset or power up will be zero. This is normal behavior.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="randval">RANDVAL</h3>
<p>Returns a random number between low and high limits such that low &lt;= N &lt; high The random number generator may first be seeded by using the SEED(number) function.</p>
<p>RANDVAL is the equivalent of aggregate functions: <code>myvar = ABS( (RAND()%(high-low)+low) );</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>RANDVAL(low, high);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">low</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Low limit for the random numbers.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">high</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">High limit for the random numbers.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A random number between low and high limits.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-273-1" name="__codelineno-273-1" href="#__codelineno-273-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">1234</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-273-2" name="__codelineno-273-2" href="#__codelineno-273-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">(),</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-273-3" name="__codelineno-273-3" href="#__codelineno-273-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-273-4" name="__codelineno-273-4" href="#__codelineno-273-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print **3558**, **1960** to the display.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The lower limit is inclusive, but the upper limit is exclusive.
If the random number generator is not seeded, the first number returned after reset or power up will be the low number in the range. This is normal behaviour.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="seed">SEED</h3>
<p>This function seeds the pseudo random number generator so it will generate a new repeatable sequence. The seed value can be a positive or negative number.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SEED(number);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">number</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the seed value for the pseudo random number generator.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-274-1" name="__codelineno-274-1" href="#__codelineno-274-1"></a><span class="n">SEED</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">-50</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-274-2" name="__codelineno-274-2" href="#__codelineno-274-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">", "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">RAND</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-274-3" name="__codelineno-274-3" href="#__codelineno-274-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-274-4" name="__codelineno-274-4" href="#__codelineno-274-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print **30129**, **27266** to the display.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sqrt">SQRT</h3>
<p>This function returns the <strong>integer square root</strong> of a number.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SQRT(number);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">number</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the positive number for the SQRT function.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The <strong>integer square root</strong> which is the greatest integer less than or equal to the square root of <strong>number</strong>.</p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-275-1" name="__codelineno-275-1" href="#__codelineno-275-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">;</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="ovf">OVF</h3>
<p>This function returns the high order 16-bits from certain math and shift functions. It is extremely useful for calculating 32-bit address offsets for MEDIA access.</p>
<p>It can be used with the shift operations, addition, subtraction, multiplication and modulus operations.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>OVF();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The high order 16-bits from certain math and shift functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-276-1" name="__codelineno-276-1" href="#__codelineno-276-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">loWord</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hiWord</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-276-2" name="__codelineno-276-2" href="#__codelineno-276-2"></a><span class="nl">loWord</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x2710</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x2710</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">                  </span><span class="c1">// (10000 * 10000 in hexformat)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-276-3" name="__codelineno-276-3" href="#__codelineno-276-3"></a><span class="nl">hiWord</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">OVF</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-276-4" name="__codelineno-276-4" href="#__codelineno-276-4"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"0x"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">hiWord</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">loWord</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-276-5" name="__codelineno-276-5" href="#__codelineno-276-5"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-276-6" name="__codelineno-276-6" href="#__codelineno-276-6"></a><span class="c1">// This example will print **0x05F5E100** to the display , which is 100,000,000 in hexadecimal</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="cy">CY</h3>
<p>This function returns the carry status of an unsigned overflow from any 16 or 32bit additions or subtractions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>CY();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Status of carry, 0 or 1.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="umul_1616">umul_1616</h3>
<p>Performs an unsigned multiply of 2 x 16bit values placing the 32bit result in a 2 word array.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>umul_1616(&amp;res32, val1, val2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">&amp;res32</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to 32bit result register.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">val1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16bit register or constant.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">val2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16bit register or constant.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the 32bit result. Carry and overflow are not affected.</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="media-functions">Media Functions</h2>
<h3 id="media_init">media_Init</h3>
<p>Initialise a uSD/SD/SDHC memory card for further operations. The SD card is connected to the SPI (serial peripheral interface) of the processor.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Init();</code>  </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if memory card is present and successfully initialised. 0 if no card is present or not able to initialise.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-285-5" name="__codelineno-285-5" href="#__codelineno-285-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">pause</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">300</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 id="media_setadd">media_SetAdd</h3>

</thead>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">LOword</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the low word (lower 2 bytes) of a 4 byte media memory byte address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 id="media_rdsector">media_RdSector</h3>
<p>Reads and Returns 512 bytes (256 words) into a destination block (e.g. <code>rdblock[256]</code>) pointed to by the internal Sector pointer. After the read the Sector pointer is automatically incremented by 1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_RdSector(Destination_Address);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Destination_Address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination block pointed to by the internal Sector pointer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if media response was TRUE. 512 bytes (256 words) in to a destination block.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-288-1" name="__codelineno-288-1" href="#__codelineno-288-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">rdblock</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">256</span><span class="p">];</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_wrsector">media_WrSector</h3>
<p>Writes 512 bytes (256 words) from a source memory block (e.g. <code>wrblock[256]</code>) into the uSD card. After the write the Sect pointer is automatically incremented by 1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_WrSector(Source_Address);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Source_Address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source memory block of 512bytes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if media response was TRUE.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-289-1" name="__codelineno-289-1" href="#__codelineno-289-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">wrblock</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">256</span><span class="p">];</span>

<a id="__codelineno-289-5" name="__codelineno-289-5" href="#__codelineno-289-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">media_SetSector</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">)</span>

<h3 id="media_readbyte">media_ReadByte</h3>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_ReadByte();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  byte value.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_readword">media_ReadWord</h3>
<p>Returns the word value (2 bytes) from the current media address. The internal byte address will then be internally incremented by two. If the address is not aligned, the word will still be read correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_ReadWord();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Returns the word value (2 bytes) from the current media address.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_writebyte">media_WriteByte</h3>
<p>Writes a byte to the current media address that was initially set with <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd()</a> or <a href="#media_setsector">media_SetSector(...)</a>; After the write operation, the Address pointer is automatically incremented by 1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_WriteByte(byte_val);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byte_val</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The lower 8-bits specifies the byte to be written at the current media address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Non-zero if write was successful.</p>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Writing bytes or words to a media sector must start from the beginning of the sector. All writes will be incremental until the <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> function is executed, or the sector address rolls over to the next sector. When <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> is called, any remaining bytes in the sector will be padded with 0xFF, destroying the previous contents. An attempt to use the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> function will result in the lower 9 bits being interpreted as zero. If the writing rolls over to the next sector, the <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> function is issued automatically internally.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_writeword">media_WriteWord</h3>
<p>Writes a word to the current media address that was initially set with <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd()</a> or <a href="#media_setsector">media_SetSector(...)</a>; After the write operation, the Address pointer is automatically incremented by 2.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_WriteWord(word_val);</code></p>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">word_val</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The 16-bit word to be written at the current media address location.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Non-zero if write was successful.</p>

<a id="__codelineno-293-26" name="__codelineno-293-26" href="#__codelineno-293-26"></a><span class="c1">// The result from the required location.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Writing bytes or words to a media sector must start from the beginning of the sector. All writes will be incremental until the <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> function is executed, or the sector address rolls over to the next sector. When <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> is called, any remaining bytes in the sector will be padded with 0xFF, destroying the previous contents. An attempt to use the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> function will result in the lower 9 bits being interpreted as zero. If the writing rolls over to the next sector, the <a href="#media_flush">media_Flush()</a> function is issued automatically internally.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="media_flush">media_Flush</h3>
<p>After writing any data to a sector, <strong>media_Flush()</strong> should be called to ensure that the current sector that is being written is correctly stored back to the media else write operations may be unpredictable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Flush();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  non-zero if OK, 0 if Failed.  </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See the <a href="#media_writebyte">media_WriteByte(..)</a> and <a href="#media_writeword">media_WriteWord(..)</a> examples.</p>
<h3 id="media_image">media_Image</h3>
<p>Displays an image from the media storage at the specified co-ordinates. The image address is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> or <a href="#media_setsector">media_SetSector(...)</a> function. If the image is shown partially off-screen, it may not be displayed correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_Image(x, y);</code></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_video">media_Video</h3>

<h3 class="page-break" id="media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame</h3>
<p>Displays a video from the media storage device at the specified co-ordinates. The video address is previously specified with the <a href="#media_setadd">media_SetAdd(..)</a> or <a href="#media_setsector">media_SetSector(...)</a> function. If the video is shown partially off it may not be displayed correctly. The frames can be shown in any order. This function gives you great flexibility for showing various icons from an image strip, as well as showing videos while doing other tasks.</p>
<p><a href="#media_videoframe">media_VideoFrame(..)</a> will now show error box for out of range video frames. Also, if frame is set to -1, just a rectangle will be drawn in background colour to blank an image. It applies to PmmC R29 or above.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>media_VideoFrame(x, y, frameNumber);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: center;">x, y</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the top left position where the video clip will be displayed.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">frameNumber</td>

<h2 class="page-break" id="memory-allocation-functions">Memory Allocation Functions</h2>
<h3 id="mem_alloc">mem_alloc</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The allocated memory contains garbage but is a fast allocation.</p>
<p>The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar)</a>;</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Alloc(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation if successful. If function fails returns a null (0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-298-1" name="__codelineno-298-1" href="#__codelineno-298-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Alloc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_allocv">mem_AllocV</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The block of memory is filled with initial signature values.</p>
<p>The block starts with A5,5A then fills with incrementing number e.g.:- A5,5A,00,01,02,03...FF,00,11....</p>
<p>This can be helpful when debugging. The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_AllocV(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Value is the pointer (Word) to the allocation if successful. If function fails returns a null (0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-299-1" name="__codelineno-299-1" href="#__codelineno-299-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_AllocV</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="mem_allocz">mem_AllocZ</h3>
<p>Allocate a block of memory to pointer myvar. The block of memory is filled with zeros.</p>
<p>The block must later be released with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar)</a>;</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_AllocZ(size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes that's allocated from the heap.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Value is the pointer to the allocation if successful. If function fails returns a null (0).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-300-1" name="__codelineno-300-1" href="#__codelineno-300-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_AllocZ</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_realloc">mem_Realloc</h3>
<p>The function may move the memory block to a new location, in which case the pointer to the new location is returned.</p>
<p>The content of the memory block is preserved up to the least of the new and old sizes, even if the block is moved.</p>
<p>If the new size is larger, the value of the newly allocated portion is indeterminate.</p>
<p>In case that ptr is NULL, the function behaves exactly as <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc()</a>, assigning a new block of size bytes and returning a pointer to the beginning of it.</p>
<p>In case that the size is 0, the memory previously allocated in ptr is deallocated as if a call to <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(myvar)</a> was made, and a NULL pointer is returned.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Realloc(ptr, size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the new location to reallocate the memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes of the block.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to the new object location.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-301-1" name="__codelineno-301-1" href="#__codelineno-301-1"></a><span class="nl">newptr</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Realloc</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myptr</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="mem_free">mem_free</h3>
<p>The function de-allocates a block of memory previously created with <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc(...)</a>, <a href="#mem_allocv">mem_AllocV(...)</a> or <a href="#mem_allocz">mem_AllocZ(...)</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Free(allocation);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">allocation</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the location of memory block to free up.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Non-zero if function is successful, 0 if the function fails.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-302-1" name="__codelineno-302-1" href="#__codelineno-302-1"></a><span class="nl">test</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Free</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="mem_heap">mem_Heap</h3>
<p>Returns byte size of the largest chunk of memory available in the heap.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Heap();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The largest available byte memory chunk in the heap.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-303-1" name="__codelineno-303-1" href="#__codelineno-303-1"></a><span class="nl">howmuch</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Heap</span><span class="p">();</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="mem_set">mem_Set</h3>
<p>Fill a block of memory with a byte value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Set(ptr, char, size);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the value to fill the block with.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the size of the block in Bytes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The pointer.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-304-1" name="__codelineno-304-1" href="#__codelineno-304-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">];</span>

<a id="__codelineno-304-5" name="__codelineno-304-5" href="#__codelineno-304-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">mem_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mh">0x55</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                  </span><span class="c1">//Only fills half of</span>
<a id="__codelineno-304-6" name="__codelineno-304-6" href="#__codelineno-304-6"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="k">for</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="k">sizeof</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="n">i</span><span class="o">++</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">//Show what is in the buffer</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="mem_copy">mem_Copy</h3>
<p>Copy a word aligned block of memory from source to destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Copy(source, destination, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">source</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the source memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the destination memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the size of the blocks in bytes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Source.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-305-1" name="__codelineno-305-1" href="#__codelineno-305-1"></a><span class="nl">myptr</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mem_Copy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ptr1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">ptr2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The count is a byte count, this facilitates comparing word aligned byte arrays when using word aligned packed strings.
Source can be a string constant e.g. 
``` cpp
myptr := mem_Copy("TEST STRING", ptr2, 12);
````</p>
</div>
<h3 id="mem_compare">mem_Compare</h3>
<p>Compare two blocks of memory <strong>ptr1</strong> and <strong>ptr2</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_Compare(ptr1, ptr2, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the 1st memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the 2nd memory block.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of bytes to compare.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  </p>
<ul>
<li>0 if we have a match</li>
<li>-1 if ptr1 &lt; ptr2</li>
<li>+1 if ptr2 &gt; ptr1. (The comparison is done alphabetically)</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
