</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="mem_arrayop1">mem_ArrayOp1</h3>
<p>This function (and the similar <a href="#mem_arrayop2">mem_ArrayOp2</a> function) can be used to perform highly optimised operation against an array of data. <a href="#mem_arrayop1">Mem_ArrayOp1</a> is for Single Arrays.</p>
<p>Single Word Array Operations:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pre-Defined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_NOP</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">No operation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_SET</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"set" the entire array with "value".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_AND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"and" the entire array with "value".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_IOR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"inclusive or"  the entire array with "value".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_XOR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"exclusive or"  the entire array with "value".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_ADD</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">signed add each element of entire array with "value"&gt;</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_SUB</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">signed subtract "value" from each element of entire array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_MUL</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">signed multiply each element of entire array with "value".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_DIV</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">8</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">signed divide each element of entire array by "value".</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_REV</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">9</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">reverse the elements of an array (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_SHL</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">10</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">shift an array left by "value" positions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_SHR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">11</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">shift an array right by "value" positions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_ROL</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">12</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">rotate an array left by "value" positions.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_ROR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">13</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">rotate an array right by "value" positions.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>Graphics only Operations:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pre-Defined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_GRAY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">14</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">convert an array of RGB565 elements to grayscale, "value" is ignored.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_WHITEN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">15</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">saturate an array of RGB565 elements to white, "value" determines saturation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_BLACKEN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">16</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">saturate an array of RGB565 elements to black, "value" determines saturation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_LIGHTEN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">17</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">increase luminance of an array of RGB565 elements, "value" determines saturation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP1_DARKEN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">18</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">decrease luminance of an array of RGB565 elements, "value" determines saturation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_ArrayOp1(memarray, count, op, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">memarray</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the array to be operated on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Size of the  array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">op</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">One of the constants defining the operation to be performed (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Value that may be required by the selected operation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="mem_arrayop2">mem_ArrayOp2</h3>
<p>This function (and the similar <a href="#mem_arrayop1">mem_ArrayOp1</a> function) can be used to perform highly optimised operation against an array of data. <a href="#mem_arrayop2">Mem_ArrayOp2</a> is for Dual Arrays.</p>
<p>Boolean and Maths Operations:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pre-Defined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_AND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"and" arrays, result to array1 (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_IOR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"inclusive or" arrays, result to array1 (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_XOR</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"exclusive or" arrays, result to array1 (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_ADD</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">4</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"add" arrays, result to array1, array1 + (array2+value).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_SUB</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">5</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"subtract" array2 from array1, result to array1, array1-(array2+value).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_MUL</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">6</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"multiply" arrays, result to array1 (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_DIV</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">7</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"divide array1 by array2" , result to array1 (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_COPY</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">8</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">"copy" array2 to array1 (value is ignored).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>Graphics only Operations:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Pre-Defined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Value</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">OP2_BLEND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">9</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">blend arrays, blend percentage determined by "value", result to "array1".</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>mem_ArrayOp2(memarray1, memarray2, count, op, value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">memarray1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the 1st array to be operated on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">memarray2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the 2nd array to be operated on.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Size of the array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">op</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">One of the constants defining the operation to be performed (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Value that may be required by the selected operation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-308-1" name="__codelineno-308-1" href="#__codelineno-308-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">a1</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">a2</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">5</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>

<h2 class="page-break" id="miscellaneous-system-functions">Miscellaneous System Functions</h2>
<h3 id="sys_pmmc">sys_PmmC</h3>
<p>Prints the system PmmC name and revision e.g. "DIABLO-16\n1.0"</p>
<p>Can be captured to a buffer using the <a href="#to">to()</a> function</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_Pmmc();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-309-1" name="__codelineno-309-1" href="#__codelineno-309-1"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myString</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_PmmC</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="c1">// save PmmC name and revision to buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_driver">sys_Driver</h3>
<p>Prints the system driver name and date string e.g. "uLCD-32WDTU-A\n130411”</p>
<p>Can be captured to a buffer using the <a href="#to">to()</a> function</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_Driver();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-310-1" name="__codelineno-310-1" href="#__codelineno-310-1"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_Driver</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">     </span><span class="c1">// save Driver name and date to buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="serial-uart-functions">Serial (UART) Functions</h2>
<h3 id="com_rx_pin">COM_RX_pin</h3>
<p>Use this function to specify which GPIO is going to be assigned to the relative com ports receive line.</p>
<p>If the pin argument is 0 the function has no effect.</p>
<p>The pin is automatically set to an input. If the COMx RX pin is set to same pin as COMx TX pin (e.g. for a loopback check) it is necessary to configure the input pin first.</p>

</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Baud rates each have degree of accuracy for several reasons. The actual baud rate you would receive and relevant error% compared to the setting value, can be calculated.</p>
<p>ActualBaud is calculated using the following formula: <code>ActualBaud = 4375000/(trunc(4375000/RequiredBaud))</code></p>
<p>Example for 115200 is, 4375000/115200 = 37.977, Trucated is 37. 4375000/37 = 118243 (rounded). <br>
Error% therefore is % difference between 115200 and 118243, therefore 2.64%</p>
<p>It is desirable to only use a baud rate between 2 devices which has a difference of typically &lt; 2%. Note both devices will have a degree of error, not just this 4D Processor, both need to be considered.</p>
</div>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>

<p>As of the v1.1 PmmC several ‘low’ values have special meanings</p>
<ol>
<li>2187500 baud</li>
<li>1458333 baud</li>
<li>1093750 baud</li>
<li>875000 baud</li>
<li>729167 baud</li>
</ol>
<p>Baud rates each have degree of accuracy for several reasons. The actual baud rate you would receive and relevant error% compared to the setting value, can be calculated.</p>
<p>Actual Baud is calculated using the following formula: </p>
<p>Actual Baud = 4375000/(trunc(4375000/RequiredBaud)) </p>
<p>Example for 115200 is, 4375000/115200 = 37.977, Trucated is 37. 4375000/37 = 118243 (rounded).</p>
<p>Error% therefore is % difference between 115200 and 118243, therefore 2.64% </p>
<p>It is desirable to only use a baud rate between 2 devices which has a difference of typically &lt; 2%. Note both devices will have a degree of error, not just this 4D Processor, both need to be considered.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="serin">serin</h3>
<p><strong>serin():</strong> Receives a character from the Serial Port COM0.
<br><strong>serin1():</strong> Receives a character from the Serial Port COM1.
<br><strong>serin2():</strong> Receives a character from the Serial Port COM2.
<br><strong>serin3():</strong> Receives a character from the Serial Port COM3.</p>
<p>serin may be buffered (refer to <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> functions). If it is desired to be able to receive the BREAK signal using buffered functions then the <a href="#com_initbrk">com_InitBrk()</a> function must be used instead.</p>
<p>The transmission format is:
<strong>No Parity, 1 Stop Bit, 8 Data Bits</strong> (N,8,1).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>serin();</code> or <code>serin1();</code> or <code>serin2();</code> or <code>serin3();</code>  </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A positive value 0 to 255 for a valid character received.<br>-1 if no character is available. <br>-2 if a framing error or over-run has occurred (auto cleared). <br>-3 (BREAK) if a break signal is detected. </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-315-1" name="__codelineno-315-1" href="#__codelineno-315-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-315-2" name="__codelineno-315-2" href="#__codelineno-315-2"></a><span class="nl">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">serin</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">//test the com 0 port</span>
<a id="__codelineno-315-3" name="__codelineno-315-3" href="#__codelineno-315-3"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&gt;=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// if a valid character is received</span>
<a id="__codelineno-315-4" name="__codelineno-315-4" href="#__codelineno-315-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">process</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="kt">char</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">  </span><span class="c1">// process the character</span>
<a id="__codelineno-315-5" name="__codelineno-315-5" href="#__codelineno-315-5"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>COM0 pins cannot be mapped, and are fixed as pins 42(Rx0) and 33(Tx0) on the DIABLO-16 chip. Rx and Tx of COM1, COM2 or COM3 should be defined before using <strong>serin1()</strong>, <strong>serin2()</strong> or <strong>serin3()</strong>.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="serout">serout</h3>
<p><strong>serout():</strong> Transmits a single byte to the Serial Port COM0.
<br><strong>serout1():</strong> Transmits a single byte to the Serial Port COM1.
<br><strong>serout2():</strong> Transmits a single byte to the Serial Port COM2.
<br><strong>serout3():</strong> Transmits a single byte to the Serial Port COM3.</p>
<p><br>The transmission format is:
<br><strong>No Parity, 1 Stop Bit, 8 Data Bits (N,8,1)</strong>.
<br>Unless <a href="#com_mode">com_Mode()</a> has been used to alter it.</p>
<p>serout may be buffered (refer to <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(..)</a> functions). If it is desired to be able to transmit the BREAK signal using buffered functions then the <a href="#com_txbufferbrk">com_TXbufferBrk()</a> function must be used instead.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>serout(char);</code> or <code>serout1(char);</code> or <code>serout2(char);</code> or <code>serout3(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the data byte to be sent to the serial port.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-316-1" name="__codelineno-316-1" href="#__codelineno-316-1"></a><span class="n">serout</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'\n'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// send a linefeed to COM0.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>COM0 pins cannot be mapped, and are fixed as pins 42(Rx0) and 33(Tx0) on the DIABLO-16 chip. Rx and Tx of COM1, COM2 or COM3 should be defined before using <strong>serout1()</strong>, <strong>serout2()</strong> or <strong>serout3()</strong>.</p>
<p>The BREAK signal can be transmitted using the predefined constant BREAK as the char to serout().</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_init">com_Init</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications buffered service. Once initialised, the service runs in the background capturing and buffering serial data without the user application having to constantly poll the serial port. This frees up the application to service other tasks.</p>
<p><strong>MODES OF OPERATION</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>No qualifier – simple ring buffer (aka circular queue)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p>If the <strong>qualifier</strong> is set to zero, the <strong>buffer</strong> is continually active as a simple circular queue. Characters when received from the host are placed in the circular queue (at the 'head' of the queue) Bytes may be removed from the circular queue (from the 'tail' of the queue) using the <a href="#serin">serin()</a> function. If the tail is the same position as the head, there are no bytes in the queue, therefore <a href="#serin">serin()</a> will return <strong>-1</strong>, meaning no character is available, also, the <a href="#com_count">com_Count()</a> function can be read at any time to determine the number of characters that are waiting between the tail and head of the queue. If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the internal <code>COM_FULL</code> flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full">com_Full()</a> function) . Any further characters from the host are now discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable. This is a good way of reading a fixed size packet and not necessarily considered to be an error condition. If no characters are removed from the buffer until the COM_FULL flag (which can be read with the <a href="#com_full">com_Full()</a> function) becomes set, it is guaranteed that the bytes will be ordered in the <strong>buffer</strong> from the start position, therefore, the <strong>buffer</strong> can be treated as an array and can be read directly without using serin() at all. In the latter case, the correct action is to process the data from the buffer, re-initialise the buffer with the <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> function, or reset the buffered serial service by issuing the <a href="#com_reset">com_Reset()</a> function (which will return serial reception to polled mode) , and send an acknowledgement to the host (traditionally a <strong>ACK</strong> or 6) to indicate that the application is ready to receive more data and the previous 'packet' has been dealt with, or conversely, the application may send a negative acknowledgement to indicate that some sort of error occurred, or the action could not be completed (traditionally a <strong>NAK</strong> or 16) .</p>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal COM_ERROR flag will be set (which can be read with the <a href="#com_error">com_Error()</a> function). Note that the COM_FULL flag will remain latched to indicate that the buffer did become full, and is not reset (even if all the characters are read) until the <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a> or <a href="#com_reset">com_Reset()</a> function is issued.</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Using a qualifier</strong></li>
</ul>
<p>If a <strong>qualifier</strong> character is specified, after the buffer is initialised with <a href="#com_initt">com_Init(..)</a> , the service will ignore all characters until the <strong>qualifier</strong> is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. After that point, the behaviour is the same as above for the 'non-qualified' mode.</p>
<p><br><strong>com_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier):</strong> Initialize a serial capture buffer for COM0.
<br><strong>com1_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier):</strong> Initialize a serial capture buffer for COM1.
<br><strong>com2_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier):</strong> Initialize a serial capture buffer for COM2.
<br><strong>com3_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier):</strong> Initialize a serial capture buffer for COM3.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com1_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com2_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com3_Init(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the background buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes). If the buffer size is zero, a buffer of 128 words (256 bytes) should be provided for automatic packet length mode (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the qualifying character that must be received to initiate serial data reception and buffer write. A zero (0x00) indicates no qualifier to be used.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="com_reset">com_Reset</h3>
<p>Resets the serial communications buffered service and returns it to the default polled mode.
<br><strong>com_Reset()</strong> Reset COM0
<br><strong>com1_Reset()</strong> Reset COM1
<br><strong>com2_Reset()</strong> Reset COM2
<br><strong>com3_Reset()</strong> Reset COM3</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Reset();</code> or <code>com1_Reset();</code> or <code>com2_Reset();</code> or <code>com3_Reset();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_count">com_Count</h3>
<p>Can be read at any time (when in buffered communications is active) to determine the number of characters that are waiting in the buffer.</p>
<p><br><strong>com_Count();</strong> Charcters countr in COM0
<br><strong>com1_Count();</strong> Charcters countr in COM1
<br><strong>com2_Count();</strong> Charcters countr in COM2
<br><strong>com3_Count();</strong> Charcters countr in COM3</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Count();</code> or <code>com1_Count();</code> or <code>com2_Count();</code> or <code>com3_Count();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Current count of characters in the communications buffer.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-319-1" name="__codelineno-319-1" href="#__codelineno-319-1"></a><span class="nl">n</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">           </span><span class="c1">// get the number of chars available in the buffer</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_full">com_Full</h3>
<p>If the queue is not read frequently by the application, and characters are still being sent by the host, the head will eventually catch up with the tail setting the COM_FULL flag which is read with this function. If this flag is set, any further characters from the host are discarded, however, all the characters that were buffered up to this point are readable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Full();</code> or <code>com1_Full();</code> or <code>com2_Full();</code> or <code>com3_Full();</code> </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if buffer or queue has become full, or is overflowed, else returns 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-320-1" name="__codelineno-320-1" href="#__codelineno-320-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Full</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">&amp;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">com_Count</span><span class="p">()</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">==</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-320-2" name="__codelineno-320-2" href="#__codelineno-320-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">com_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">30</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// buffer full, recovery</span>
<a id="__codelineno-320-3" name="__codelineno-320-3" href="#__codelineno-320-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="com_error">com_Error</h3>
<p>If any low level errors occur during the buffering service (such as framing or over-run) the internal <strong>COM_ERROR</strong> flag will be set which can be read with this function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Error();</code> or <code>com1_Error();</code> or <code>com2_Error();</code> or <code>com3_Error();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if any low level communications error occurred, else returns 0</p>

<h3 id="com_sync">com_Sync</h3>
<p>If a <strong>qualifier</strong> character is specified when using buffered communications, after the buffer is initialized with <a href="#com_init">com_Init(..)</a>, <strong>com1_Init(..)</strong>, <strong>com2_Init(..)</strong>, or <strong>com3_Init(..)</strong> the service will ignore all characters until the qualifier is received and only then initiate the buffer write sequence with incoming data. <strong>com_Sync()</strong>, <strong>com1_Sync()</strong>, <strong>com2_Sync()</strong>, <strong>com3_Sync()</strong> is called to determine if the qualifier character has been received yet.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Sync();</code> or <code>com1_Sync();</code> or <code>com2_Sync();</code> or <code>com3_Sync();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  1 if the qualifier character has been received, else returns 0.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-322-1" name="__codelineno-322-1" href="#__codelineno-322-1"></a><span class="nl">stat</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">com_Sync</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// See if the qualifier is received at COM0</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer</h3>
<p>Initialise a serial buffer for the <strong>COM0</strong>, <strong>COM1</strong>, <strong>COM2</strong> or <strong>COM3</strong> output. The program must declare a var array as a circular buffer. When a TX buffer is declared for comms, the transmission of characters becomes non-blocking. If the buffer has insufficient space to accept the next character from a <a href="#serout">serout(..)</a>, serout1(..), serout2(..) or serout3(..) function, the excess characters will be ignored, and the <a href="#com_fulll">com_Full()</a>, com1_Full(), com2_Full() or com3_Full() error will be asserted. If the TX buffer is no longer required, just set the buffer pointer to zero, the size in this case doesn't matter and is ignored. The function can be resized or reallocated to another buffer at any time. The buffer is flushed before any changes are made.</p>
<p>"pin" designates an IO pin to control a bidirectional control device for half duplex mode. "pin" will go HI at the start of a transmission, and will return low after the final byte is transmitted.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code> or <code>com1_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code> or <code>com2_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code> or <code>com3_TXbuffer(buf, bufsize, pin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 2 bytes).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the turnaround pin. If not required, just set "pin" to zero.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-323-1" name="__codelineno-323-1" href="#__codelineno-323-1"></a><span class="n">com_TXbuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">1024</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA1</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">            </span><span class="c1">// set the TX buffer of COM0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-323-2" name="__codelineno-323-2" href="#__codelineno-323-2"></a><span class="n">com_TXbuffer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                      </span><span class="c1">// revert COM0 to non buffered service</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_txbufferhold">com_TXbufferHold</h3>
<p>This function is used in conjunction with <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(...)</a>, com1_TXbufferHold(ON), com2_TXbufferHold(ON) or
com3_TXbufferHold(ON).</p>
<p>It is often necessary to hold off sending serial characters until a complete frame or packet has been built in the output buffer. <strong>com_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong>, <strong>com1_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong>, <strong>com2_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong>, <strong>com3_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong> is used for this, to stop the buffer being sent while it is being loaded. Normally, when using buffered comms, the transmit process will begin immediately. This is fine unless you are trying to assemble a packet.</p>
<p>To build a packet and send it later, issue a com_TXbufferHold(ON), com1_TXbufferHold(ON), com2_TXbufferHold(ON), com3_TXbufferHold(ON) build the packet, when packet is ready, issuing com_TXbufferHold(OFF), com1_TXbufferHold(OFF), com2_TXbufferHold(OFF), com3_TXbufferHold(OFF) will release the buffer to the com port.</p>
<p>Also, if using <a href="#com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</a>, <strong>com1_TXemptyEvent</strong>, <strong>com2_TXemptyEvent</strong>, <strong>com3_TXemptyEvent</strong>, erroneous empty events will occur as the transmit buffer is constantly trying to empty while you are busy trying to fill it.</p>
<p>Also refer to the pin control for <a href="#com_txbufferr">com_TXbuffer(..)</a>, <strong>com1_TXbuffer(..)</strong>, <strong>com2_TXbuffer(..)</strong>, or <strong>com3_TXbuffer(..)</strong> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXbufferHold(state);</code> or <code>com1_TXbufferHold(state);</code> or <code>com2_TXbufferHold(state);</code> or <code>com3_TXbufferHold(state);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">state</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the state of the buffer used for the buffering service.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  </p>
<ul>
<li>Buffer count when called with argument of 1, for example <strong>com_TXbufferHold(ON)</strong></li>
<li>-1 if function is called illegally when TX comms is not buffered.</li>
<li>0 when argument is zero, e.g. <strong>com_TXbufferHold(OFF)</strong></li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: Refer to the <a href="#com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress)</a> example.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you fill the buffer whilst it is held comms error 4 will be set and the data written will be lost.</p>
</div>

<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Count of characters.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="com_txemptyevent">com_TXemptyEvent</h3>
<p>If a comms TX buffer that was previously allocated with <a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(..)</a>, <strong>com1_TXbuffer(..)</strong>, <strong>com2_TXbuffer(..)</strong>, or <strong>com3_TXbuffer(..)</strong>. This function can be used to set up a function to be called when the <strong>COM0</strong>, <strong>COM1</strong>, <strong>COM2</strong> or <strong>COM3</strong> TX buffer is empty.</p>
<p>This is useful for either reloading the TX buffer, setting or clearing a pin to change the direction of e.g. a RS485 line driver, or any other form of traffic control. The event function must not have any parameters. To disable the event, simply call <strong>com_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong>, <strong>com1_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong> ,
<strong>com2_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong> or <strong>com3_TXemptyEvent(0)</strong>.</p>
<p><a href="#com_txbuffer">com_TXbuffer(..)</a>, <strong>com1_TXbuffer(..)</strong>, <strong>com2_TXbuffer(..)</strong>, or <strong>com3_TXbuffer(..)</strong> also resets any active event.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress);</code> or <code>com1_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress);</code> or <code>com2_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress);</code> or <code>com3_TXemptyEvent(functionAddress);</code></p>

</tr>

</table></div></div>

</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="com_mode">com_Mode</h3>
<p>Use this function to set the required serial port parameters to other than 8N1.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_Mode("databits", "parity", "Stopbits", "comport");</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">databits</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of databits, 8 is the only currently valid value.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">parity</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the parity bit. Valid values are N(one), E(ven) and O(dd).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Stopbits</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the number of stop bits. Valid values are 1 and 2.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">comport</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the Com port <strong>COM0</strong>, <strong>COM1</strong>, <strong>COM2</strong>, <strong>COM3</strong>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if the parameters were acceptable.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="com_rxblock">com_RXblock</h3>
<p>Bufsize bytes are received from the serial port to the string pointer "buf". If a receive buffer is active and bufsize characters are available this function will return almost immediately otherwise it will block until the required bytes are received. This function is useful for protocols that require the reading of a fixed amount of data in one hit. Once the data has been read into a buffer it also makes it easy to perform CRC calculations on the data.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_RXblock("buf", "bufsize");</code> or <code>com1_RXblock("buf", "bufsize");</code> or <code>com2_RXblock("buf", "bufsize");</code> or <code>com3_RXblock("buf", "bufsize");</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String Pointer address of buffer to receive the data.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The number of characters to receive into the buffer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="com_txblock">com_TXblock</h3>
<p>Bufsize bytes are transmitted to the serial port from the string pointer "buf". This function is useful for protocols that require the reading of a fixed amount of data in one hit. Once the data has been read into a buffer it also makes it easy to perform CRC calculations on the data.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="com_initbrk">com_InitBrk</h3>
<p>This is the initialisation function for the serial communications buffered service with the ability to receive the BREAK signal as though it is a character. The parameters are identical to <a href="#com_init">com_Init()</a> except that each buffer entry can now only hold one byte. The BREAK ‘character’ is is a predefined constant call BREAK.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>com_InitBrk(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com1_InitBrk(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com2_InitBrk(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code> or <code>com3_InitBrk(buffer, bufsize, qualifier);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buffer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the address of a buffer used for the background buffering service.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the byte size of the user array provided for the buffer (each array element holds 1 byte). If the buffer size is zero, a buffer of 128 words (256 bytes) should be provided for automatic packet length mode (see below).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">qualifier</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the qualifying character that must be received to initiate serial data reception and buffer write. A zero (0x00) indicates no qualifier to be used.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None        </p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-329-1" name="__codelineno-329-1" href="#__codelineno-329-1"></a><span class="n">com_InitBrk</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">combuf</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">20</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">//set up a comms ring buffer for COM0 , 10 characters before overflow</span>
</code></pre></div>

<h2 class="page-break" id="sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</h2>
<h3 id="snd_volume">snd_Volume</h3>
<p>Set the sound playback volume. Var must be in the range from 8 (min volume) to 127 (max volume). If var is less than 8, volume is set to 8, and if var &gt; 127 it is set to 127.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Volume(var);</code></p>

<td style="text-align: left;">sound playback volume.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="snd_freq">snd_Freq</h3>
<p>Produces a pure square wave waveform on the audio output pin. This command is designed to drive Piezo transducers which require this sort of input. Whilst it also works on displays with a builtin amplifier the sound produced is extremely annoying.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>snd_Freq(frequency, duration);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">frequency</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The frequency of the sound to produce, 10Hz is the minimum.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">duration</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The duration of the sound in milli seconds.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if freq &gt;= 10 and a wav file is not currently playing.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-338-1" name="__codelineno-338-1" href="#__codelineno-338-1"></a><span class="n">snd_Freq</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2731</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// produce a 100ms burst at the Piezo’s resonant frequency.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h2 class="page-break" id="spi-control-functions">SPI Control Functions</h2>
<p>The SPI functions in this section apply to any general purpose SPI device.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>SPI0 is connected internally to the uSD card. <a href="#spi_init">spi_Init()</a>, <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a>, <a href="#spi_write">spi_Write()</a> and <a href="#spi_disable">spi_Disable()</a> all refer to the SPI0 to communicate with the uSD card through direct SPI commands. Only adept users should attempt this as it might damage the uSD card.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spi_init">spi_Init</h3>
<p>Sets up the DIABLO-16 SPI port to communicate with the uSD card through direct SPI commands. It should not be used if uSD card is active. See the example in section <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Init(speed, address_mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the speed of the SPI port. <br><strong>SPI_FAST</strong> – 16Mhz <br><strong>SPI_MED</strong> – 4Mhz <br><strong>SPI_SLOW</strong> – 650Khz</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address_mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sets the address mode of the SPI port. <br><strong>0</strong> – Set address_mode to 0 when dealing with 16MB or less <br><strong>SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4</strong> – Set to this if dealing with Flash larger than 16MB.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-339-1" name="__codelineno-339-1" href="#__codelineno-339-1"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_FAST</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">                       </span><span class="c1">// init SPI at maximum speed for 16MB Flash</span>
<a id="__codelineno-339-2" name="__codelineno-339-2" href="#__codelineno-339-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-339-3" name="__codelineno-339-3" href="#__codelineno-339-3"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SLOW</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">       </span><span class="c1">// init SPI at Slow speed for 32MB</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Address_mode needs to be <strong>SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4</strong> for flash devices with more than 16MB of capacity (to enable 4 byte addressing), else 0 for standard 3 byte addressing.</p>
<p>This is only for the uSD Card, it is <strong>not</strong> for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonition warning">
<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
<p>This should not be tampered with for normal operation, as the DIABLO-16 handles the uSD card itself. Only use if you are an adept user and know what you are doing.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spi_read">spi_Read</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte read from the uSD card via SPI.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A single data byte from the uSD card via SPI.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-340-1" name="__codelineno-340-1" href="#__codelineno-340-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-340-2" name="__codelineno-340-2" href="#__codelineno-340-2"></a><span class="n">spi_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">              </span><span class="c1">// 650 kHZ, RXMODE_0, CKMODE_0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-340-3" name="__codelineno-340-3" href="#__codelineno-340-3"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Hello World</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">// replace with your code</span>
<a id="__codelineno-340-4" name="__codelineno-340-4" href="#__codelineno-340-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-340-5" name="__codelineno-340-5" href="#__codelineno-340-5"></a><span class="c1">//....</span>
<a id="__codelineno-340-6" name="__codelineno-340-6" href="#__codelineno-340-6"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-340-7" name="__codelineno-340-7" href="#__codelineno-340-7"></a><span class="n">spi_Write</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mh">0x40</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-340-8" name="__codelineno-340-8" href="#__codelineno-340-8"></a><span class="nl">result</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">spi_Read</span><span class="p">();</span>
<a id="__codelineno-340-9" name="__codelineno-340-9" href="#__codelineno-340-9"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"result: "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">result</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This is only for the uSD Card, it is <strong>not</strong> for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</p>
<p>The Chip Select line (SDCS) is lowered automatically.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonition warning">
<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
<p>This should not be tampered with for normal operation, as the DIABLO-16 handles the uSD card itself. Only use if you are an adept user and know what you are doing.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spi_write">spi_Write</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte write to the uSD card via SPI.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Write(byte);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byte</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the data byte to be sent to the uSD card via SPI.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See the example in section <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a>.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This is only for the uSD Card, it is <strong>not</strong> for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</p>
<p>The Chip Select line (SDCS) is lowered automatically.</p>
</div>
<div class="admonition warning">
<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
<p>This should not be tampered with for normal operation, as the DIABLO-16 handles the uSD card itself. Only use if you are an adept user and know what you are doing.</p>
</div>
<h3 id="spi_disable">spi_Disable</h3>
<p>This function raises the Chip Select (SDCS) line of the uSD card, disabling it from further activity. The CS line will be automatically lowered next time the SPI functions <a href="#spi_read">spi_Read()</a> or <a href="#spi_write">spi_Write(...)</a> are used, and also by the action of any <a href="#media-functions">media_functions</a>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_Disable();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>
TODO</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This is only for the uSD Card, it is <strong>not</strong> for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spi1_init">SPI1_Init</h3>
<p>Initialize the SPI port to communicate with the SPI device. There are three peripheral interface SPI ports that can be used to communicate with three different SPI devices with different speeds and modes at the same time. SPI1, SPI2 and SPI3 need to be initialized separately using PI1_Init(..),
SPI2_Init(..) or SPI3_Init(..) functions.</p>

<p>Mode can also be “OR’ed” with SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4 when SPI Flash memory is used which requires 4 byte addressing.</p>
<p>This is only required for Flash chips having a capacity of greater than 16MB, thus requiring more than he standard 3 byte addressing. Refer to the Datasheet of the Flash Memory in question.</p>
<p>The syntax would be for example <code>SPI8_MODE_0 | SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4</code>, in place of the ‘mode’ argument.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SPI1_Init(speed, mode, enablepin);</code> or <code>SPI2_Init(speed, mode, enablepin);</code> or <code>SPI3_Init(speed, mode, enablepin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">speed</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the speed of the SPI port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the mode of SPI operation.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The DIABLO-16 pin connected to CS on the relevant chip.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  True if the function succeeded.</p>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-341-1" name="__codelineno-341-1" href="#__codelineno-341-1"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI1_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SPEED15</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI8_MODE_5</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-341-2" name="__codelineno-341-2" href="#__codelineno-341-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"INIT parameter Invalid n"</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-341-3" name="__codelineno-341-3" href="#__codelineno-341-3"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
<a id="__codelineno-341-4" name="__codelineno-341-4" href="#__codelineno-341-4"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-341-5" name="__codelineno-341-5" href="#__codelineno-341-5"></a><span class="k">if</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="o">!</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI3_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SPEED12</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI16_MODE_3</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">|</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA2</span><span class="p">))</span>
<a id="__codelineno-341-6" name="__codelineno-341-6" href="#__codelineno-341-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"INIT parameter Invalid n"</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-341-7" name="__codelineno-341-7" href="#__codelineno-341-7"></a><span class="n">endif</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This is only for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3, it is separate from the spi_Init() function used for the uSD Card.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spi1_read">SPI1_Read</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte read from the SPI device connected to SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3 port. A dummy write using all bits set is automatically written to the SPI port to being the read.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SPI1_Read();</code> or <code>SPI2_Read();</code> or <code>SPI3_Read();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A single data byte from the SPI device.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-342-1" name="__codelineno-342-1" href="#__codelineno-342-1"></a><span class="cp">#CONST</span>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The Chip Select line needs to be manually lowered and raised by the users’ code since this pin is determined by the user and is not a fixed pin.</p>
<p>This is only for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3, it is separate from the spi_Read() function used for the uSD Card</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="spi1_write">SPI1_Write</h3>
<p>This function allows a raw unadorned byte write to the SPI device connected to SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3 port.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>SPI1_Write(byte);</code> or <code>SPI2_Write(byte);</code> or <code>SPI3_Write(byte);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">byte</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the data byte to be sent to the SPI device.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The data read from the SPI port whilst the write is in progress.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in section “<a href="#spi1_read">SPI1_Read()</a>”</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The Chip Select line needs to be manually lowered and raised by the users’ code since this pin is determined by the user and is not a fixed pin.</p>
<p>This is only for SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3, it is separate from the spi_Write() function used for the uSD Card.</p>
</div>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Only a single pin should be mapped to spi SCK. If the pin argument is 0 the previously selected spi SCK pin is disconnected. The pin is automatically set to an output.</p>
<p>Some 4D Systems display modules utilise this pin for additional peripherals such as Resistive or Capacitive Touch. To ensure that the pin is available for use, refer to the appropriate product’s datasheet.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spi1_sdi_pin">SPI1_SDI_pin</h3>

<h3 class="page-break" id="spi_readblock">spi_ReadBlock</h3>
<p>Bufsize bytes are read from the SPI port to the string pointer "buf". This function gives much better performance than reading individual bytes at a time. Once the data has been read into a buffer it also makes it easy to perform CRC calculations on the data. The SPI port must be initialised in 8-bit mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spi_ReadBlock("buf", "bufsize");</code> or <code>spi1_ReadBlock("buf", "bufsize");</code> or <code>spi2_ReadBlock("buf", "bufsize");</code> or <code>spi3_ReadBlock("buf", "bufsize");</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">buf</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String Pointer address of buffer to receive the data.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">bufsize</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The number of characters to receive into the buffer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="spi_writeblock">spi_WriteBlock</h3>

<h2 class="page-break" id="spi-flash-functions">SPI Flash Functions</h2>
<p>These functions can be used to access an SPI FLASH storage device connected to the selected SPI port, and correctly initialised with the <a href="#spi_init">spi_Init(...)</a> function, each FLASH device also needs a dedicated enable pin pulled high and set as output from within the driving program. Devices like the M25Pxx and A25Lxx which has 512Kbit to 128Mbit of Serial Flash Memory are supported. Other similar devices should work. Additionally, support for more than 16MB of serial flash is available by using SPI_ADDRESS_MODE4 in the relevant SPI Init function.</p>
<p>Sample initialization code:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-346-1" name="__codelineno-346-1" href="#__codelineno-346-1"></a><span class="cp">#CONST</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-2" name="__codelineno-346-2" href="#__codelineno-346-2"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">EnablePin</span><span class="w">   </span><span class="n">PA0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-3" name="__codelineno-346-3" href="#__codelineno-346-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">ClockPin</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">PA6</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-4" name="__codelineno-346-4" href="#__codelineno-346-4"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">SDIPin</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">PA2</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-5" name="__codelineno-346-5" href="#__codelineno-346-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">SDOPin</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="n">PA5</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-6" name="__codelineno-346-6" href="#__codelineno-346-6"></a><span class="cp">#END</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-7" name="__codelineno-346-7" href="#__codelineno-346-7"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-346-8" name="__codelineno-346-8" href="#__codelineno-346-8"></a><span class="n">pin_HI</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">EnablePin</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-9" name="__codelineno-346-9" href="#__codelineno-346-9"></a><span class="n">pin_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">PIN_OUT</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">EnablePin</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-10" name="__codelineno-346-10" href="#__codelineno-346-10"></a><span class="n">SPI1_SDI_pin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SDIPin</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-11" name="__codelineno-346-11" href="#__codelineno-346-11"></a><span class="n">SPI1_SCK_pin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">ClockPin</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-12" name="__codelineno-346-12" href="#__codelineno-346-12"></a><span class="n">SPI1_SDO_pin</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SDOPin</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-346-13" name="__codelineno-346-13" href="#__codelineno-346-13"></a><span class="n">SPI1_Init</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI_SPEED15</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI8_MODE_5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">EnablePin</span><span class="p">)</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">;</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>When accessing certain file types via spiflash it may be necessary to append an identifiable EOF character (e.g. ^Z) to enable your program to properly detect EOF.</p>
<p>The Init must be done in 8-bit mode, but the internal functions will automatically flip between 8 and 16-bit mode to gain optimal performance.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_blockerase">spiflash_BlockErase</h3>
<p>Erases the required block in a FLASH media device. The function returns no value, and the operation can take up to 3 milliseconds.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_BlockErase(spi#, Enablepin, block);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">block</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The block to be erased.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-347-1" name="__codelineno-347-1" href="#__codelineno-347-1"></a><span class="n">spiflash_BlockErase</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">3</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="spiflash_bulkerase">spiflash_BulkErase</h3>
<p>Erases the entire flash media device. The function returns no value, and the operation can take up to 80 seconds depending on the size of the flash device. Note that not all devices support this command.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_BulkErase(spi#, Enablepin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-348-1" name="__codelineno-348-1" href="#__codelineno-348-1"></a><span class="n">spiflash_BulkErase</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_exec">spiflash_Exec</h3>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#spiflash_run">spiflash_Run</a>, however, the main program in FLASH retains all memory allocations (e.g. file buffers, memory allocated with <a href="#mem_alloc">mem_Alloc</a> etc.)</p>
<p>Returns like a function, current program calling program is kept active and control returns to it.</p>
<p>If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else arglist points to an array, the first element being the number of elements in the array.</p>
<p>func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments.</p>
<p>This function is similar to <a href="#spiflash_loadfunction">spiflash_LoadFunction(...)</a>, however, the function argument list is passed by pointer, and the memory consumed by the function is released as soon as the function completes.</p>
<p><a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd</a> should have previously been called to identify the address of the program to be called.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_Exec(spi#, Enablepin, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program or 0 if no arguments.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-349-1" name="__codelineno-349-1" href="#__codelineno-349-1"></a><span class="n">spiflash_Exec</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_getc">spiflash_GetC</h3>
<p>Reads a character (or byte) from the SPI FLASH memory device on the specified SPI port and enable pin. The source is the address set by <a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd()</a>, or incremented by subsequent reads or writes.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_GetC(spi#, Enablepin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The next char from the file.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-350-1" name="__codelineno-350-1" href="#__codelineno-350-1"></a><span class="nl">mychar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">spiflash_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_gets">spiflash_GetS</h3>
<p>This function Reads a line of text to a buffer (specified by "*string") from the FLASH memory device on the specified SPI port and enable pin into the specified destination. The source is the address set by <a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd()</a>, or incremented by subsequent reads or writes.</p>
<p><a href="#file_gets">file_GetS(...)</a> will stop reading when any of the following conditions are true:</p>
<p>a. It has read n-1 bytes (one character is reserved for the null-terminator).
b. It encounters a newline character (a line-feed in the compilers tested here).
c. It reaches the end of file
d. A read error occurs.</p>
<p>The file must be previously opened with 'r' (read) mode.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_GetS(*String, size, spi#, Enablepin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">size</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The maximum number of bytes to be read from the file. (Up to max of 80).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The number of characters read from file (excluding the null terminator).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-351-1" name="__codelineno-351-1" href="#__codelineno-351-1"></a><span class="nl">res</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">spiflash_GetS</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mystring</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">80</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">SPI1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Only reads up to "size-1" characters into "string".</p>
</div>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_loadfunction">spiflash_LoadFunction</h3>
<p>Load a function or program from the FLASH memory device on the specified SPI port and enable pin at the address set by <a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd()</a>, or incremented by subsequent reads or writes and return a function pointer to the allocation.</p>
<p>The function can then be invoked just like any other function would be called via a function pointer. Parameters may be passed to it in a conventional way. The function may be discarded at any time when no longer required, thus freeing its memory resources.</p>
<p>The loaded function can be discarded with <a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(..)</a>. </p>
<p>The callers stack is shared by the loaded function, however any global variables in the loaded function are private to that function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_LoadFunction(spi#, Enablepin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the memory allocation where the function has been loaded from file which can be then used as a function call.</p>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Any pointer references passed to the child function may not include references to the parents DATA statements or any static string references. Any string or array information must be in the parents global or local memory space. The reason for this is that DATA statements and static strings are contained in the parents CODE segment, and cannot be accessed by the child process.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_loadimagecontrol">spiflash_LoadImageControl</h3>
<p>Reads a control file to create an image list from the FLASH memory device on the specified SPI port and enable pin. The source is the address set by <a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd()</a>, or incremented by subsequent reads or writes. The ".dat" file is first and is immediately followed by a ^Z and then the ".gci' file.</p>
<p>When an image control is loaded, an array is built in ram. It consists of a 6 word header with the following entries as defined by the constants:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">value</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_COUNT</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_ENTRYLEN</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">1</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_MODE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">2</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_GCI_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">3</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_DAT_FILENAME</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">4</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">IMG_GCIFILE_HANDLE</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">5</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>No images are stored in FLASH or RAM, the image control holds the index values for the absolute storage positions on the uSD card for RAW mode, or the cluster/sector position for formatted FAT16 mode.</p>
<p>When an image control is no longer required, the memory can be released with:
<a href="#mem_free">mem_Free(MyImageControlHandle);</a></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_LoadImageControl(spi#, Enablepin) ;</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A handle (pointer to the memory allocation) to the image control list that has been created. NULL if function fail.</p>
