<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_playwav">spiflash_PlayWAV</h3>
<p>Play a wave file from the FLASH memory device on the specified SPI port and enable pin. The source is the address set by <a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd()</a>, or incremented by subsequent reads or writes. Opens the wav file, decode the header to set the appropriate wave player parameters and set off the playing of the file as a background process.</p>
<p>This function automatically grabs a chunk of memory for a wave buffer. The minimum memory requirement is the wave buffer size of 1024. The size of the wave buffer allocation can be increased by the <a href="#snd_bufsize">snd_BufSize</a> function.</p>
<p>The default size 1024 bytes.</p>
<p>See “<a href="#sound-control-functions">Sound Control Functions</a>” for additional play control functions.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_PlayWAV(spi#, Enablepin);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  </p>
<ul>
<li>If there are no errors, returns number of blocks to play (1 to 32767). </li>
<li>If errors occurred, the following is returned <ul>
<li>-7 : Insufficient memory available for WAV buffer and file.</li>
<li>-6 : cant play this rate.</li>
<li>-5 : no data chunk found in first rsector.</li>
<li>-4 : no format data.</li>
<li>-3 : no wave chunk signature.</li>
<li>-2 : bad wave file format.</li>
<li>-1 : file not found.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-358-1" name="__codelineno-358-1" href="#__codelineno-358-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">ding.wav</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-358-2" name="__codelineno-358-2" href="#__codelineno-358-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-358-3" name="__codelineno-358-3" href="#__codelineno-358-3"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="k">for</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">:=</span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">&lt;</span><span class="mi">45</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">n</span><span class="o">++</span><span class="p">)</span>
<a id="__codelineno-358-4" name="__codelineno-358-4" href="#__codelineno-358-4"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="nl">pitch</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">NOTES</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">n</span><span class="p">];</span>
<a id="__codelineno-358-5" name="__codelineno-358-5" href="#__codelineno-358-5"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">([</span><span class="n">UDEC</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">pitch</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\r</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-358-7" name="__codelineno-358-7" href="#__codelineno-358-7"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="n">spiflash_PlayWAV</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SPI1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">PA0</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-358-8" name="__codelineno-358-8" href="#__codelineno-358-8"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="k">while</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">snd_Playing</span><span class="p">());</span>
<a id="__codelineno-358-9" name="__codelineno-358-9" href="#__codelineno-358-9"></a><span class="w">        </span><span class="c1">//pause(500);</span>

</code></pre></div>

<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The memory is only required during the duration of play, and is automatically released while not in use.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="spiflash_run">spiflash_Run</h3>
<p>Any memory allocations in the main FLASH program are released, however, the stack and globals are maintained.</p>
<p>If arglistptr is 0, no arguments are passed, else arglistptr points to an array, the first element being the number of additional elements in the array which contain the arguments.</p>
<p>func 'main' in the called program accepts the arguments, if any.</p>
<p>The arguments can only be passed by value, no pointers or references can be used as all memory is cleared before the file is loaded. Refer to <a href="#spiflash_exec">spiflash_Exec</a> and <a href="#spiflash_loadfunction">spiflash_LoadFunction</a> for functions that can pass by reference.</p>
<p><a href="#spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd</a> should have previously been called to identify the address of the program to be called.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_Run(spi#, Enablepin, arglistptr);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Enablepin</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The enable pin assigned to this spiflash device, e.g. PA0.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">arglistptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer to the list of arguments to pass to the new program.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The value from main in the called program.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: Refer to the <a href="#file_run">file_Run</a> example.</p>
<h3 id="spiflash_setadd">spiflash_SetAdd</h3>
<p>Set media memory internal Address pointer for to SPI FLASH memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>spiflash_SetAdd(spi#, HiWord, LoWord);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">spi#</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The SPI port to use, e.g. SPI0, SPI1, SPI2 or SPI3.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">HiWord</td>

</table></div></div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="str_match">str_Match</h3>
<p>Case Sensitive match.
Compares the string at position ptr in a string buffer to the string str, skipping over any leading spaces prior to the test. If a match occurs, ptr is advanced to the first position past the match, else ptr is not altered</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Match(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Address of byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Pointer string to match.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if no match, else advance ptr to the next position after the match and returns a pointer to the match position.</p>

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_MatchI(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>

</tr>
</tbody>

<h3 class="page-break" id="str_find">str_Find</h3>
<p>Case Sensitive.
Given the address of a pointer to a source string as the first argument, and a pointer to a test string as the second argument, attempts to find the position of the matching string in the source string. The test is performed with case sensitivity.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Find(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String to find.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if not found. Returns the address of the first character of the match if successful.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="str_findi">str_FindI</h3>
<p>Case Insensitive.
Given the address of a pointer to a source string as the first argument, and a pointer to a test string as the second argument, attempts to find the position of the matching string in the source string. The test is performed with case insensitivity, e.g. upper and lower case chars are accepted.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_FindI(&amp;ptr, *str);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to string buffer.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">String to find.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  0 if not found. Returns the address of the first character of the match if successful.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="str_printf">str_Printf</h3>
<p>This function prints a formatted string from elements derived from a structured byte region. There is only one input argument, the byte region pointer ptr which is automatically advanced as the format specifier string is processed. The format string is similar to the C language, however, there are a few differences, including the addition of the indirection token * (asterix).</p>
<p>Format Specifiers:</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">format</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%c</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">character</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%s</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">string of characters</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%d</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">signed decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%ld</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">long decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%u</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">unsigned decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%lu</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">long unsigned decimal</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%x</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">hex byte</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%X</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">hex word</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%lX</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">hex long</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%b</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">binary word</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">%lb</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">long binary word</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p>(*) indirection prefix (placed after '%' to specify indirect addressing)</p>
<p>(number) width description (use between '%' and format specifier to set the field width).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Printf(&amp;ptr, *format);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Byte pointer to the input data (structure).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">format</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Format string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The position of last extraction point. This is useful for processing by other string functions.</p>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The address of the pointer must be passed so the function can advance it as required.
The format specifier string can be a string pointer, allowing dynamic construction of the printing format.
If (number) is preceded by 0, the result is Left-pads with zeroes (0) instead of spaces.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="str_cat">str_Cat</h3>
<p>Appends a copy of the source string to the destination string. The terminating null character in destination is overwritten by the first character of source, and a new null-character is appended at the end of the new string formed by the concatenation of both in destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Cat(&amp;destination, &amp;source);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">destination</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination string address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">source</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source string address.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to the destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-389-10" name="__codelineno-389-10" href="#__codelineno-389-10"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">repeat</span>

</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="str_catn">str_CatN</h3>
<p>The number of characters copied is limited by "count".
The terminating null character in destination is overwritten by the first character of source, and a new null-character is appended at the end of the new string formed by the concatenation of both in destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_CatN(&amp;ptr, str, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ptr</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Destination string address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">str</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Source string address.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of characters to be concatenated.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Pointer to the destination.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="str_bytemove">str_ByteMove</h3>
<p>Copy bytes from "src" to "dest", stopping only when "count" is exhausted. No terminator is appended, it is purely a byte copy, and any zeroes encountered will also be copied.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_ByteMove(src, dest, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Number of bytes to transfer.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the end of the destination (which is "dest" + "count").</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-391-1" name="__codelineno-391-1" href="#__codelineno-391-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">src</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">dest</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">],</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">mybuf2</span><span class="p">[</span><span class="mi">10</span><span class="p">];</span><span class="w">      </span><span class="c1">// string pointers and two 20 byte buffers</span>
<a id="__codelineno-391-2" name="__codelineno-391-2" href="#__codelineno-391-2"></a><span class="n">to</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">putstr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"TESTING 123"</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-391-4" name="__codelineno-391-4" href="#__codelineno-391-4"></a><span class="nl">src</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strPtr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf1</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
<a id="__codelineno-391-5" name="__codelineno-391-5" href="#__codelineno-391-5"></a><span class="nl">dest</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Ptr</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">mybuf2</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-391-6" name="__codelineno-391-6" href="#__codelineno-391-6"></a><span class="n">src</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">+=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">6</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">                                   </span><span class="c1">// move src pointer to "G 123"</span>

<a id="__codelineno-391-9" name="__codelineno-391-9" href="#__codelineno-391-9"></a>

<a id="__codelineno-391-11" name="__codelineno-391-11" href="#__codelineno-391-11"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-391-12" name="__codelineno-391-12" href="#__codelineno-391-12"></a><span class="nl">nextpos</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_ByteMove</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="str_copy">str_Copy</h3>
<p>Copy a string from "src" to "dest", stopping only when the end of source string "src" is encountered (0x00 terminator). The terminator is always appended, even if "src" is an empty string.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_Copy(dest, src);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">dest</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  A pointer to the 0x00 string terminator at the end of "dest" (which is "dest" + str_Length(src); ).</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-392-1" name="__codelineno-392-1" href="#__codelineno-392-1"></a><span class="nl">nextplace</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">str_Copy</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">d</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="str_copyn">str_CopyN</h3>
<p>Copy a string from "src" to "dest", stopping only when "count" is exhausted, or end of source string "str" is encountered (0x00 string terminator). The terminator is always appended, even if "count" is zero, or "src" is a null string.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>str_CopyN(dest, src, count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned destination.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">src</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Points to byte aligned source.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Maximum number of bytes to copy.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>

<h2 class="page-break" id="system-memory-functions">System Memory Functions</h2>
<h3 id="peekw">peekW</h3>
<p>Read a word from system memory.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>peekW(address);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The address of a memory word. The address is usually a pre-defined system register address constant, (see the address constants for all the system word sized registers in <a href="#system-registers-memory">System Register Memory</a>).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The 16-bit value stored at <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-394-1" name="__codelineno-394-1" href="#__codelineno-394-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-394-2" name="__codelineno-394-2" href="#__codelineno-394-2"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">peekW</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">SYSTEM_TIMER_LO</span><span class="p">);</span>

<a id="__codelineno-394-4" name="__codelineno-394-4" href="#__codelineno-394-4"></a><span class="c1">// This example places the low word of the 32-bit system timer in myvar.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The <a href="#txt_set">txt_Set</a> variables (0-15) and <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_set</a> variables (16-31) can also be accessed with peekW and pokeW.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="pokew">pokeW</h3>
<p>This function writes a 16-bit value to a location specified by <strong>address</strong>.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>pokeW(address, word_value);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">Address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The address of a memory word. The address is usually a pre-defined system register address constant, (see the address constants for all the system word sized registers in <a href="#system-registers-memory">System Register Memory</a>).</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">word_value</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The 16-bit word_value will be stored at <strong>address</strong>.</td>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-395-3" name="__codelineno-395-3" href="#__codelineno-395-3"></a><span class="c1">// This example sets TIMER2 to 5 seconds.</span>

<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>the <a href="#txt_set">txt_Set</a> variables (0-15) and <a href="#gfx_set">gfx_set</a> variables (16-31) can also be accessed with peekW and pokeW.</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="text-and-string-functions">Text and String Functions</h2>
<h3 id="txt_movecursor">txt_MoveCursor</h3>
<p>Moves the text cursor to a screen position set by line and column parameters. The line and column position is calculated, based on the size and scaling factor for the currently selected font. When text is outputted to screen it will be displayed from this position. The text position could also be set with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(...)</a>; if required to set the text position to an exact pixel location. Note that lines and columns start from 0. So, line 0, column 0 is the top left corner of the display.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>txt_MoveCursor(line, column);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">line</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required line position.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">column</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required column position.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-396-1" name="__codelineno-396-1" href="#__codelineno-396-1"></a><span class="n">txt_MoveCursor</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">4</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">9</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-396-2" name="__codelineno-396-2" href="#__codelineno-396-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-396-3" name="__codelineno-396-3" href="#__codelineno-396-3"></a><span class="c1">// This example moves the text origin to the 5th line and the 10th column.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>This function sets the TEXT_MARGIN the x value, this is so you can easily left align text using <code>\n</code>. If you don’t want this, simply set TEXT_MARGIN to 0 using <a href="#pokew">pokeW(TEXT_MARGIN,0)</a>.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="putch">putch</h3>
<p><strong>putch</strong> prints single characters to the current output stream, usually the display.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putch(char);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Holds a positive value for the required character.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="putstr">putstr</h3>
<p><strong>putstr</strong> and, similarly <a href="#print">print([STR]x)</a>; operate on constant strings in Flash, or word aligned strings in RAM.</p>
<p><strong>putstr</strong> prints a string to the current output stream, usually the display.</p>
<p>A string constant is automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>A string in a data statement is not automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>All variables in 4DGL are 16bit, if an array is used for holding 8-bit characters; each array element packs 1 or 2 characters.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putstr(string);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant, a word pointer to a string, a pointer to an array, or a pointer to a data statement. Note that for a byte aligned RAM string you need to use <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a>.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The pointer to the item that was printed.</p>

<h3 class="page-break" id="putstrxy">putstrXY</h3>
<p><strong>putstrXY</strong> prints a string at position x, y on the display.</p>
<p>A string constant is automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>A string in a data statement is not automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>All variables in 4DGL are 16bit, if an array is used for holding 8-bit characters; each array element packs 1 or 2 characters.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putstrXY(xpos, ypos, string);</code></p>

</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xpos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal position of the string.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">ypos</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical position of the string.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant, a word pointer to a string, a pointer to an array, or a pointer to a data statement. Note that for a byte aligned RAM string you need to use <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a> in conjunction with <a href="#gfx_moveto">gfx_MoveTo(x,y)</a> command.</td>
</tr>

<a id="__codelineno-404-18" name="__codelineno-404-18" href="#__codelineno-404-18"></a><span class="n">wend</span>
</code></pre></div>

<div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--prev" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div><div class="tabbed-control tabbed-control--next" hidden=""><button class="tabbed-button" tabindex="-1" aria-hidden="true"></button></div></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="putstrcentred">putstrCentred</h3>
<p><strong>putstrCentred</strong> prints a string centered at position x, y on the display.</p>
<p>A string constant is automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>A string in a data statement is not automatically terminated with a zero.</p>
<p>All variables in 4DGL are 16bit, if an array is used for holding 8-bit characters; each array element packs 1 or 2 characters.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>putstrCentred(xc, yc, string);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">xc</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the horizontal position of the string.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">yc</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Specifies the vertical position of the string.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">string</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">A string constant, a pointer to a string, a pointer to an array, or a pointer to a data statement.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-405-1" name="__codelineno-405-1" href="#__codelineno-405-1"></a><span class="n">putstrCentred</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">120</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">0</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"4D Lab's</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// Print 4D Labs centered at 120, 0</span>
<a id="__codelineno-405-2" name="__codelineno-405-2" href="#__codelineno-405-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-405-3" name="__codelineno-405-3" href="#__codelineno-405-3"></a><span class="c1">// Assuming X-resolution = 240, this command will print ‘4D Labs’ in the top-middle of the screen.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>The string constants and data statement pointers are byte aligned.</p>
</div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="putnum">putnum</h3>

<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-406-1" name="__codelineno-406-1" href="#__codelineno-406-1"></a><span class="n">var</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-406-2" name="__codelineno-406-2" href="#__codelineno-406-2"></a><span class="nl">v</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mo">0567</span><span class="mi">8</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-406-3" name="__codelineno-406-3" href="#__codelineno-406-3"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">HEX</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// print the number as hex 4 digits</span>
<a id="__codelineno-406-4" name="__codelineno-406-4" href="#__codelineno-406-4"></a><span class="n">putnum</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">BIN</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">v</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">//print the number as binary 16 digits</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="print">print</h3>
<p><strong>4DGL</strong> has a versatile <a href="#print">print(...)</a> statement for formatting numbers and strings. In its simplest form, print will simply print a number as can be seen below:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-407-1" name="__codelineno-407-1" href="#__codelineno-407-1"></a><span class="nl">myvar</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">100</span><span class="p">;</span>
<a id="__codelineno-407-2" name="__codelineno-407-2" href="#__codelineno-407-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-407-3" name="__codelineno-407-3" href="#__codelineno-407-3"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-407-4" name="__codelineno-407-4" href="#__codelineno-407-4"></a><span class="c1">// This will print **100** to the current output device (usually the display in TEXT mode). </span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>If you wish to add a string anywhere within a <a href="#print">print(...)</a> statement, just place a quoted string expression and you will be able to mix strings and numbers in a variety of formats. See the following example.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-408-1" name="__codelineno-408-1" href="#__codelineno-408-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"the value of myvar is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"and its 8bit binary representation is:-"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">BIN8</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
</div>
<p>(*) Refer the table in <a href="#putnum">putnum(..)</a> for all the numeric representations available.</p>
<p>The <a href="#print">print(...)</a> statement will accept directives passed in square brackets to make it print in various ways, for instance, if you wish to print a number in 4 digit hex, use the <strong>[HEX4]</strong> directive placed in front of the variable to be displayed within the print statement. See the following example.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-409-1" name="__codelineno-409-1" href="#__codelineno-409-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"myvar as a 4 digit HEX number is :- "</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">HEX4</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>There are 2 print directives that are not part of the numeric set and will be explained separately. these are the <strong>[STR]</strong> and <strong>[CHR]</strong> directives.</p>
</div>
<p>The <strong>[STR]</strong> directive expects a string pointer to follow:</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-410-1" name="__codelineno-410-1" href="#__codelineno-410-1"></a><span class="nl">s</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"Hello World"</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// assign a string constant to s </span>
<a id="__codelineno-410-2" name="__codelineno-410-2" href="#__codelineno-410-2"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"Var 's' points to a string constant at address"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="s">" which is"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">STR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">s</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>The <strong>[CHR]</strong> directive prints the character value of a variable.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-411-1" name="__codelineno-411-1" href="#__codelineno-411-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"The third character of the string is '"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">CHR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="o">*</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">s</span><span class="o">+</span><span class="mi">2</span><span class="p">));</span>
</code></pre></div>
<p>also</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-412-1" name="__codelineno-412-1" href="#__codelineno-412-1"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"The value of 'myvar' as an ASCII charater is '"</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">[</span><span class="n">CHR</span><span class="p">]</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myvar</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>You can freely mix string pointers, strings, variables and expressions within a print statement. <a href="#print">print(...)</a> can also use the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> function to redirect it's output to a different output device other than the screen using the function (refer to the <a href="#to">to(...)</a> statement for further examples).</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>print(...);</code>    </p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-413-1" name="__codelineno-413-1" href="#__codelineno-413-1"></a><span class="cp">#platform "uLCD-70DT"</span>
<a id="__codelineno-413-2" name="__codelineno-413-2" href="#__codelineno-413-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-413-3" name="__codelineno-413-3" href="#__codelineno-413-3"></a><span class="c1">// DATA STATEMENT</span>
<a id="__codelineno-413-4" name="__codelineno-413-4" href="#__codelineno-413-4"></a><span class="cp">#DATA</span>
<a id="__codelineno-413-5" name="__codelineno-413-5" href="#__codelineno-413-5"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">word</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myData</span>
<a id="__codelineno-413-6" name="__codelineno-413-6" href="#__codelineno-413-6"></a><span class="w">    </span><span class="n">myString1</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Bert</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">Fred</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">main</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myString2</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">baud</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">barney</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x1111</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x2222</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x3333</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mh">0x4444</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="to">to</h3>
<p><a href="#to">to()</a> sends the printed output to destinations other than the screen. Normally, print just sends its output to the display in <strong>TEXT</strong> mode which is the default, however, the output from print can be sent to 'streams', e.g. – <strong>COM0</strong>, <strong>COM1</strong>, <strong>COM2</strong>, or <strong>COM3</strong>, an open FAT16 file with <strong>DSK</strong>, to raw media with <strong>MDA</strong> (media), or to the I2C ports with <strong>I2C1</strong>, <strong>I2C2</strong> or <strong>I2C3</strong>.</p>
<p>The <strong>to(...)</strong> function can also stream to a memory array . Note that once the <strong>to(...)</strong> function has taken effect, the stream reverts back to the default stream which is <strong>TEXT</strong> as soon as <a href="#putch">putch</a>, <a href="#putstr">putstr</a>, <a href="#putnum">putnum</a>, <a href="#print">print</a>, or <a href="#str_printf">str_Printf</a> has completed its action.</p>
<p>The <strong>APPEND</strong> argument is used to append the printed output to the same place as the previous redirection. This is most useful for building string arrays, or adding sequential data to a media stream.</p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Predefined Name</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Constant</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">putch, putstr, putnum, print, str_Printf redirection</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">DSK</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF802</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the most recently open file that has been opened in write mode.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM0</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF804</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM0</strong> (default serial) port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF05</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM1</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF06</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM2</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">COM3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xFF07</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirected to the <strong>COM3</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF820</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>I2C1</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF821</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>I2C2</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">I2C3</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF822</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>I2C3</strong> port.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">MDA</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0xF840</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is directed to the <strong>SD/SDHC</strong> or <strong>FLASH</strong> media.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">APPEND</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">0x0000</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is appended to user array if previous redirection was to an array.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">(memory pointer)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Array Address</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Output is redirect to the <strong>memory</strong> pointer argument.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<div class="admonition warning">
<p class="admonition-title">Warning</p>
<p>Becareful writing to a FAT16 formatted card without checking legal partitioned are, else the disk formatting will be destroyed.</p>
</div>

<h3 class="page-break" id="charwidth">charwidth</h3>
<p><strong>charwidth</strong> is used to calculate the width in pixel units for a character, based on the currently selected font.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charwidth('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the width calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a single character in pixel units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-415-1" name="__codelineno-415-1" href="#__codelineno-415-1"></a><span class="c1">// Example</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-2" name="__codelineno-415-2" href="#__codelineno-415-2"></a>
<a id="__codelineno-415-3" name="__codelineno-415-3" href="#__codelineno-415-3"></a><span class="nl">str</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">"HELLO</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">THERE"</span><span class="p">;</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="c1">// note that this string spans 2 lines due</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-4" name="__codelineno-415-4" href="#__codelineno-415-4"></a><span class="w">                                </span><span class="c1">// to the \n.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-5" name="__codelineno-415-5" href="#__codelineno-415-5"></a><span class="nl">width</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strwidth</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// get the width of the string, this will</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-6" name="__codelineno-415-6" href="#__codelineno-415-6"></a><span class="w">                                </span><span class="c1">// a lso capture the height.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-7" name="__codelineno-415-7" href="#__codelineno-415-7"></a><span class="nl">height</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strheight</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w">          </span><span class="c1">// note, invoking strwidth also calcs height</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-8" name="__codelineno-415-8" href="#__codelineno-415-8"></a><span class="w">                                </span><span class="c1">// which we can now read.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-9" name="__codelineno-415-9" href="#__codelineno-415-9"></a><span class="c1">// The string above spans 2 lines, strheight(.) will calculate height correctly for multiple lines.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-10" name="__codelineno-415-10" href="#__codelineno-415-10"></a><span class="nl">len</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">strlen</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">str</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">             </span><span class="c1">// the strlen() function returns the number of characters in a string.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-11" name="__codelineno-415-11" href="#__codelineno-415-11"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">Length="</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">len</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// NB: the \n in "HELLO \nTHERE" is counted as a character.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-12" name="__codelineno-415-12" href="#__codelineno-415-12"></a><span class="n">txt_FontID</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">MS_SanSerif8x12</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">    </span><span class="c1">// select this font</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-13" name="__codelineno-415-13" href="#__codelineno-415-13"></a><span class="nl">w</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">charwidth</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'W'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// get a characters width</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-14" name="__codelineno-415-14" href="#__codelineno-415-14"></a><span class="nl">h</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">charheight</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="sc">'W'</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// and height</span>

<a id="__codelineno-415-16" name="__codelineno-415-16" href="#__codelineno-415-16"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">'W' is "</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">w</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">" pixels wide"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// show width of a character 'W' in pixel units.</span>
<a id="__codelineno-415-17" name="__codelineno-415-17" href="#__codelineno-415-17"></a><span class="n">print</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">(</span><span class="s">"</span><span class="se">\n</span><span class="s">'W' is "</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">,</span><span class="n">h</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s">" pixels high"</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// show height of a character 'W' in pixel units.</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="charheight">charheight</h3>
<p><strong>charheight</strong> is used to calculate the height in pixel units for a character, based on the currently selected font.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>charheight('char');</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">char</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The ascii character for the height calculation.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a single character in pixel units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strwidth">strwidth</h3>
<p><strong>strwidth</strong> returns the width of a zero terminated string in pixel units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strwidth(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string. 'pointer' may be a constant or pointer to word aligned variable.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The width of a string in pixel units, can be multi line.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="strheight">strheight</h3>
<p><strong>strheight</strong> returns the height of a zero terminated string in pixel units. The strwidth function must be called first which makes available width and height. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strheight();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The height of a string in pixel units, can be multi line.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 id="strlen">strlen</h3>
<p><strong>strlen</strong> returns the length of a zero terminated string in character units. Note that any string constants declared in your program are automatically terminated with a zero as an end marker by the compiler. Any string that you create in the DATA section or MEM section must have a zero added as a terminator for this function to work correctly.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>strlen(pointer);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">pointer</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The pointer to a zero (0x00) terminated string.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The length of a string in character units.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See example in <a href="#charwidth">charwidth</a>.</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="unicode_page">unicode_page</h3>
<p>After selecting a Unicode image control with <a href="#txt_fontid">txt_FontID</a>, this function is called to set the required font within the Unicode set. The file "Unicode.inc" contains wrappers for this function, and it is not normally called directly.</p>
<p>Refer to Unicode documentation ‘4DGL-Unicode-REVx.pdf’ and ‘Unicode.inc’ for further information.</p>
<!-- TODO: Find this document -->

<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>unicode_page(charbeg, charend, charoffset);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">charbeg</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Offset of first character in Unicode set.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">charend</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Offset of ending character in Unicode Set.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">charoffset</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Offset of first ASCII character in Unicode Set.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Count of characters in the set.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong>: See Unicode.inc</p>
<h3 class="page-break" id="txt_set">txt_Set</h3>
<p>Given a function number and a value, set the required text control parameter, such as size, colour, and other formatting controls. This function is extremely useful in a loop to select multiple parameters from a data statement or a control array. Note also that each function available for <a href="#txt_set">txt_Set</a> has a <a href="#single_parameter_shortcuts">single parameter 'shortcut' function</a> that has the same effect.</p>

</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">txt_Attributes(value)</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Allows a combination of text attributes to be defined together by 'or'ing the bits together. The feature automatically resets after printing using putstr or print has completed.   <br><strong>Example:</strong> <br><code>txt_Set(TEXT_ATTRIBUTES, BOLD | INVERSE); // bold + inverse</code> <br><strong>Note:</strong> bits 0-3 and 8-15 are reserved.</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"></td>
</tr>

<td style="text-align: left;">16 or <strong>BOLD</strong> <br>32 or <strong>ITALIC</strong> <br>64 or <strong>INVERSE</strong> <br>128 or <strong>UNDERLINED</strong></td>

<tr>
<td style="text-align: left;">txt_Angle(value)</td>

<h3 class="page-break" id="sys_settimer">sys_SetTimer</h3>
<p>Set a countdown on the selected timer or 'top-up' if required. There are 8 timers TIMER0 to TIMER7 which stop at the count of 0. Maximum timeout period is 65, 535 milliseconds or 65.535 seconds. A timer can be read with the <a href="#sys_gettimer">sys_GetTimer("timernum")</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_SetTimer(timernum, value);</code></p>

</tr>

</tr>

</tr>
</tbody>

<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-421-1" name="__codelineno-421-1" href="#__codelineno-421-1"></a><span class="nl">t</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_GetTimer</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TIMER2</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="sys_settimerevent">sys_SetTimerEvent</h3>
<p>Set a function to be called for selected timer. When the timer reaches zero, the function is called. The called function must not have any parameters, and should not have a return value. This is necessary because the timer event is invoked asynchronously to the mainline program (i.e, it is not called in the normal way, so parameters and return values don’t apply).</p>
<p><a href="#sys_settimerevent">sys_SetTimerEvent(timernum, 0)</a> disables the timer event.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>When a child process is run using the file_run or file_exec function, or if a file was loaded with file_Loadfunction and is executed, the loaded process gets its own code and memory space, therefore, any timer that reaches zero that has a timer event attached in the parent code space, will fail and cause a crash as an attempt is made to force the program counter to some wild place in the child process - There are 2 ways to overcome this problem.</p>
<ol>
<li>If a child process will not be requiring the use of any timers or timer events, the parent program
can simply use the <a href="#sys_eventspostpone">eventsPostpone()</a> function before calling or entering the child process. Once the
parent program regains control, the <a href="#sys_eventsresume">eventsResume()</a> function will allow any events in the queue to
then be processed. The side effect of this method is that several events may bank up, and will execute
immediately once the <a href="#sys_eventsresume">eventsResume()</a> takes place. This however disallows a child process to use any
timer events in the sub program so method 2 is preferable in this case.</li>
<li>The parent program can 'disconnect' the event(s) by setting it/them to zero prior to child process execution, or setting the associated timer to zero so the event wont fire. In either case, it is necessary to do the following:</li>
</ol>
<p><code>while(sys_EventQueue());</code></p>
<p>to ensure the event queue is empty prior to calling the child process. Note also that if just the timer is set to zero, the child process cannot use this timer. If the timer was now set to a value and the old event still existed, when the timer reaches zero the 'bad' parent address event will fire causing a crash.</p>
<p>The reverse situation also applies of course, the same level of respect is required if a child program
needs to use any timer events. Method [1] (above) will not work as the events have been
postponed, stopping the child process from using any timer events. If the child process did an
<a href="#sys_eventsresume">eventsResume()</a> in this case, everything would crash miserably. So the same applies, a child that
uses any timer events must respect any timers that may be used by the parent, and a child must
zero the <strong>sys_SetTimerEvent</strong> before returning to the parent.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_SetTimerEvent(timernum, function);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">timernum</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">One of eight timers TIMER0 to TIMER7.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">function</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Event Function to be queued.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Any previous event function address, or zero if there was no previous function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-422-1" name="__codelineno-422-1" href="#__codelineno-422-1"></a><span class="n">sys_SetTimerEvent</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TIMER5</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">myfunc</span><span class="p">);</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="sys_eventqueue">sys_EventQueue</h3>
<p>Returns the max number of events that were pending in the event queue since the last call to this function. This can be used to assess event overhead burden, especially after or during a <a href="#sys_eventspostpone">sys_EventsPostpone</a> action.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_EventQueue();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Number of events.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-423-1" name="__codelineno-423-1" href="#__codelineno-423-1"></a><span class="nl">tasks</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">sys_EventQueue</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">//</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_eventspostpone">sys_EventsPostpone</h3>
<p>Postpone any events until the <a href="#sys_eventsresume">sys_EventResume</a> function is executed. The event queue will continue to queue events, but no action will take place until a <a href="#sys_eventsresume">sys_EventResume</a> function is encountered.
The queue will continue to receive up to 32 events before discarding any further events. This function is required to allow a sequence of instructions or functions to occur that would otherwise be corrupted by an event occurring during the sequence of instructions or functions. A good example of this is when you set a position to print, if there was no way of locking the current sequence, an event may occur which does a similar thing, and a contention would occur - printing to the wrong position. This function should be used wisely, if any action that is required would take considerable time, it is better to disable any conflicting event functions with a bypass flag, then restart the conflicting event by re-issuing a timer value.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_EventsPostpone();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-424-1" name="__codelineno-424-1" href="#__codelineno-424-1"></a><span class="n">sys_EventsPostpone</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// postpone the event queue</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="sys_eventsresume">sys_EventsResume</h3>
<p>Resume any postponed events. The queue will try to execute any events that were incurred during the postponed period. Note that queued events are only checked for and executed at the end of each 4DGL instruction.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_EventsResume();</code></p>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-425-1" name="__codelineno-425-1" href="#__codelineno-425-1"></a><span class="n">sys_EventsResume</span><span class="p">();</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// resume the event queue</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 id="sys_deepsleep">sys_DeepSleep</h3>
<p>Deep Sleep is a sleep state that is ‘deeper’ than the regular Sleep (for most display modules) and therefore consumes less power. Some displays do not support being powered to a lower state, so sleep and deepsleep power consumption can sometimes be roughly the same.</p>
<p>Puts the display and processor into the lowest power mode for a period of time. If "units" is zero, the display goes into sleep mode forever and needs power cycling to re-initialize. If "units" is 1 to 65535, the display will sleep for that period of time, or will be woken when touch screen is touched. The function returns the count of "units" that are remaining when the screen was touched. When returning from deep sleep mode, some displays might lose their screen and/or need to be reinitialised with <a href="#disp_init">disp_Init()</a>.</p>
<p><em>New in v0.7 PmmC.</em></p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_DeepSleep(units);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">units</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sleep timer units are approx 1 second. When in sleep mode, timing is controlled by an RC oscillator, therefore, timing is not totally accurate and should not be relied on for timing purposes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Remaining time units when touch screen is touched, else returns zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-426-1" name="__codelineno-426-1" href="#__codelineno-426-1"></a><span class="n">sys_DeepSleep</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">60</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// Sleep for 1 minute</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="sys_sleep">sys_Sleep</h3>
<p>Regular sleep, which puts the display and processor into low power mode for a period of time. If "units" is zero, the display goes into sleep mode forever and needs power cycling to re-initialize. If "units" is 1 to 65535, the display will sleep for that period of time, or will be woken when touch screen is touched. The function returns the count of "units" that are remaining when the screen was touched. When returning from sleep mode, the display and processor are restored from low power mode.</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p><a href="#sys_sleep">sys_Sleep()</a> was found to have an issue in PmmC’s prior to R33, the units value was not always near 1 second. This has been corrected in PmmC R33.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>sys_Sleep(units);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">units</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">Sleep timer units are approx 1 second. When in sleep mode, timing is controlled by an RC oscillator, therefore, timing is not totally accurate and should not be relied on for timing purposes.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Remaining time units when touch screen is touched, else returns zero.</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="touch-screen-functions">Touch Screen Functions</h2>
<h3 id="touch_detectregion">touch_DetectRegion</h3>
<p>Specifies a new touch detect region on the screen. This setting will filter out any touch activity outside the region and only touch activity within that region will be reported by the status poll <a href="#touch_get">touch_Get(TOUCH_STATUS)</a> function.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>touch_DetectRegion(x1, y1, x2, y2);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the horizontal position of the top left corner of the region.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y1</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the vertical position of the top left corner of the region.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">x2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the horizontal position of the bottom right corner of the region.</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">y2</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">specifies the vertical position of the bottom right corner of the region.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>

<a id="__codelineno-435-2" name="__codelineno-435-2" href="#__codelineno-435-2"></a><span class="n">touch_DetectRegion</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="mi">101</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">101</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">,</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="mi">200</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w">         </span><span class="c1">// limit touch detect region towithin the rectangle</span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="touch_set">touch_Set</h3>
<p>Sets various Touch Screen related parameters.</p>
<p><strong>mode = TOUCH_ENABLE (Mode 0)</strong> Enable Touch Screen.</p>
<p><code>touch_Set(TOUCH_ENABLE);</code> - Enables and initialises Touch Screen hardware</p>
<p><strong>mode = TOUCH_DISABLE (Mode 1)</strong> Disable Touch Screen.</p>
<p><code>touch_Set(TOUCH_DISABLE);</code> - Disables the Touch Screen.</p>
<p><strong>mode = TOUCH_REGIONDEFAULT (Mode 2)</strong> Default Touch Region.</p>
<p><code>touch_Set(TOUCH_REGIONDEFAULT);</code> - This will reset the current active region to default which is the full screen area</p>
<div class="admonition note">
<p class="admonition-title">Note</p>
<p>Touch Screen task runs in the background and disabling it when not in use will free up extra resources for 4DGL CPU cycles.</p>
</div>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>touch_Set(mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>mode = TOUCH_ENABLE</strong> <br><strong>mode = TOUCH_DISABLE</strong> <br> <strong>mode = TOUCH_REGIONDEFAULT</strong></td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  None</p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong></p>
<div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code><a id="__codelineno-436-1" name="__codelineno-436-1" href="#__codelineno-436-1"></a><span class="n">touch_Set</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TOUCH_ENABLE</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// </span>
</code></pre></div>
<h3 class="page-break" id="touch_get">touch_Get</h3>
<p>Returns various Touch Screen parameters to caller.
Sometimes NOTOUCH can be returned when the touchscreen is touched and held (in between pressed and released). This occurs if the touch points are identical on two successive calls, because it does not qualify as MOVING, but it has not yet been RELEASED (but has already been PRESSED)</p>
<p><strong>mode = TOUCH_STATUS (Mode 0)</strong> - Returns the various states of the touch screen</p>
<ul>
<li>0 = NOTOUCH</li>
<li>1 = TOUCH_PRESSED</li>
<li>2 = TOUCH_RELEASED</li>
<li>3 = TOUCH_MOVING</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>mode = TOUCH_GETX (Mode 1)</strong> - Returns the X coordinates of the touch reported by mode 0</p>
<p><strong>mode = TOUCH_GETY (Mode 2)</strong> - Returns the Y coordinates of the touch reported by mode 0</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>touch_Get(mode);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">mode</td>
<td style="text-align: left;"><strong>mode = TOUCH_STATUS (Mode 0):</strong> Get Status <br><strong>mode = TOUCH_GETX (Mode 1) :</strong> Get X coordinates <br><strong>mode = TOUCH_GETY (Mode 2) :</strong> Get Y coordinates</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  The various states of the touch screen <br><strong>0 = NOTOUCH</strong> <br><strong>1 = TOUCH_PRESSED</strong> <br><strong>2 = TOUCH_RELEASED</strong> <br><strong>3 = TOUCH_MOVING</strong></p>
<p><strong><em>Example</em></strong> <br>
</p><div class="highlight"><pre><span></span><code tabindex="0"><a id="__codelineno-437-1" name="__codelineno-437-1" href="#__codelineno-437-1"></a><span class="nl">state</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">touch_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TOUCH_STATUS</span><span class="p">);</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="c1">// get touchscreen status</span>
<a id="__codelineno-437-2" name="__codelineno-437-2" href="#__codelineno-437-2"></a><span class="nl">x</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">touch_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TOUCH_GETX</span><span class="p">);</span>
<a id="__codelineno-437-3" name="__codelineno-437-3" href="#__codelineno-437-3"></a><span class="nl">y</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="p">:</span><span class="o">=</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="n">touch_Get</span><span class="p">(</span><span class="n">TOUCH_GETY</span><span class="p">);</span>

<h3 class="page-break" id="touch_testarea">touch_TestArea</h3>
<p>The touch_TestArea function creates a test area based on the parameters in <strong>rect</strong>, and returns true if the last touch resided within the test area.</p>
<p><strong>rect</strong> is an array of 4 vars, x1, y1, x2, y2 (using absolute co-ordinates).</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>touch_TestArea(&amp;rect);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>
<th style="text-align: center;">Arguments</th>
<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">rect</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">An array of 4 vars, x1, y1, x2, y2 (using absolute co-ordinates).</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  TRUE if last touch co-ordinates are within the absolute co-ordinate test area.</p>

<h2 class="page-break" id="widget-functions">Widget Functions</h2>
<h3 id="widget_create">widget_Create</h3>
<p>Creates a widget control capable of holding count elements and returns a handle for the control.</p>
<p><strong><em>Syntax</em></strong>:   <code>widget_Create(count);</code></p>
<div class="md-typeset__scrollwrap"><div class="md-typeset__table"><table>
<thead>
<tr>

<th style="text-align: left;">Description</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr>
<td style="text-align: center;">count</td>
<td style="text-align: left;">The number of elements in the widget control.</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table></div></div>
<p><strong><em>Returns</em></strong>:  Widget control handle.</p>
